roster.name: Jaxon Smith-Njigba
roster.outlook: Jaxon Smith-Njigba will look to continue his dominant campaign in Seattle's Week 12 matchup versus San Francisco. Prior to the Seahawks' Week 11 bye, Smith-Njigba had one of his biggest games of the season, posting an 8-171-1 receiving line against the Raiders. The talented wideout has worked with QB Drew Lock over Seattle's past two games, but Sam Darnold (quad/ribs) is expected to be back for this Sunday's NFC West clash. Smith-Njigba recorded 102 receiving yards and a touchdown when Seattle and San Francisco battled in Week 5, and the 49ers have given up 11 receiving TDs to wideouts this season, tied for eighth-most in the NFL.

roster.name: Saquon Barkley
roster.outlook: Saquon Barkley carried the offensive load for the Eagles last game, though exited the contest due to a left arm issue. Barkley rushed 17 times for 75 yards and a touchdown, though did not log a carry during the final eight minutes of the narrow 19-16 win over the Steelers. Barkley should be healthy enough to suit up on Thanksgiving versus the Cowboys, though. Dallas has been abysmal against the run in 2026, allowing 151.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is the worst mark in the NFL. In addition, the Cowboys have given up 15 rushing scores, which is 29th in the league.

roster.name: Rashee Rice
roster.outlook: Rashee Rice continues to handle a steady role in the Kansas City passing attack. Over four games since returning from a hamstring injury, the fourth-year wide receiver has caught at least five passes each time out, producing a 23-237-1 line on 27 targets. Patrick Mahomes appears to be back in peak form, but that hasn't yet translated into a ceiling game for Rice, who has yet to haul in more than 88 yards in any game this year and has only two touchdowns in eight appearances. Rice will look to break out in Week 12 against a Bills secondary that's tied for 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Colston Loveland
roster.outlook: Colston Loveland will seek to keep it rolling in Week 12 as the Bears play the Lions. Loveland found the end zone again in Week 11 against the Saints, pairing his touchdown with three catches for 29 yards. The second-year tight end has now put together a 27-282-3 receiving line over the last five games after a shaky start to the season. Detroit has allowed the most fantasy points per game to the TE position.

roster.name: Jadarian Price
roster.outlook: Jadarian Price's role at running back for Seattle could gain further clarity in Week 12 against San Francisco. Though he scored his first career touchdown in Week 10 against Las Vegas, Price's 10 touches lagged well behind those of Zach Charbonnet, who rushed 20 times for 94 yards. Seattle was on bye Week 11, so if Charbonnet again gets the lion's share of work this weekend, it could be an indication that Price is locked into the team's No. 2 RB role. Both he and Charbonnet could face tough sledding against a 49ers defense that has given up the fourth-fewest yards per carry (3.55) to running backs this season.

roster.name: Jameson Williams
roster.outlook: Jameson Williams will seek to keep it rolling as the Lions play the Bears in Week 12. Williams led Detroit in receiving yards against the Buccaneers in Week 11, bringing in all four of his targets for 93 yards and a touchdown. The speedster has now posted a 36-611-6 receiving line across 10 games, and he's logged 50 or more yards in four of his last five outings. He'll face a Chicago defense that's ranked a tough 10th in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.

roster.name: Parker Washington
roster.outlook: Parker Washington had a career-high 152 receiving yards and a touchdown on seven receptions against the Titans in Week 10, and he'll face the AFC South's cellar-dwellers again in Week 12, this time in Jacksonville. Another fantasy WR1 performance is on the table for Washington against Tennessee's reeling secondary, which has allowed the most catches and receiving yards to wideouts this season. The Titans are giving up 16 catches for 210 yards and 1.1 TDs per game to WRs, while Washington leads the Jaguars with a 44-748-6 receiving line through 10 games, with two of his three 100-yard receiving performances this season coming in the last two weeks.

roster.name: Zach Charbonnet
roster.outlook: Zach Charbonnet appears to have seized the lead-RB role for Seattle heading into a Week 12 matchup against the 49ers. Charbonnet didn't debut until Week 8 against Chicago and had just nine touches in that game, but in his most recent appearance -- Week 10 versus Las Vegas -- he carried 20 times for 94 yards while logging a season-high 72% offensive snap share. Jadarian Price should continue to factor into the backfield mix as well, but there's a good chance that Charbonnet will be the leader of the team's backfield moving forward. He'll face a tough test against the 49ers, who have given up the fourth-fewest fantasy points per game (14.0) to running backs this season.

roster.name: KC Concepcion
roster.outlook: KC Concepcion and the Browns are home for a Week 12 clash against Las Vegas on Sunday Night Football. He corralled three of eight targets for 21 yards and rushed once for a six-yard TD during Cleveland's Week 10 victory. Concepcion finished second on the team in targets but was sixth in yardage, although he salvaged the outing with his first career rushing score. He draws a winnable matchup versus a Raiders defense allowing 33.5 fantasy points per game to opposing WRs.

roster.name: Denzel Boston
roster.outlook: Denzel Boston and the Browns host the 4-7 Raiders on Sunday Night Football in Week 12. He brought in one of two targets for 16 yards during Cleveland's 27-24 win in Week 10. Boston struggled while appearing to aggravate a toe injury in the victory, but hopefully, the rookie has had enough time to get close to 100% following the team's bye. Boston will aim to find the end zone for the first time since Week 5 against a Las Vegas defense that's given up 13 TDs to the position, tied for fourth most in the league.

roster.name: Emmett Johnson
roster.outlook: Emmett Johnson has taken full advantage of Kenneth Walker's absence from the Kansas City backfield due to a groin strain. Over two games with Walker on the sideline, Johnson has erupted for 206 rushing yards and a touchdown while adding a 10-108-2 line on 11 targets. While the rookie running back will return to the No. 2 role once Walker is cleared to return, Johnson's performance could encourage Andy Reid to use more of a timeshare between them in order to keep both fresh ahead of the playoffs. Walker is expected to return in Week 12 against the Bills, but Johnson might be able to make a difference on limited touches against a defense that ranks 21st in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

roster.name: Chase McLaughlin
roster.outlook: Chase McLaughlin could receive few scoring chances during Tampa Bay's Week 12 matchup against the Panthers. McLaughlin didn't attempt a field goal during the Week 11 loss to the Lions but converted on all three of his extra points. On the season, the veteran has been perfect, making all 22 of his field-goal tries and all 21 of his point-after attempts. Despite his impressive season, Carolina has held opponents to just 7.1 kicking points per game, making this an unfavorable matchup for McLaughlin.

roster.name: Bo Nix
roster.outlook: Bo Nix didn't need to do much in the Broncos' Week 11 win over the Raiders, as rookie running back Jonah Coleman carried the offense. Nix has thrown for 240-plus yards just once all season, and he's produced more than two TDs only once, as the Denver offense has mostly been stuck in neutral. Coleman's emergence could provide Nix with the security he needs to try to throw downfield more often. The third-year quarterback will take on a Steelers defense in Week 12 that ranks fifth in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

roster.name: Kirk Cousins
roster.outlook: Kirk Cousins will look to bounce back in Week 12 as the Vikings play the Falcons. Cousins struggled against the 49ers for the second time this season, throwing for 235 yards with zero touchdowns and one interception in a Week 11 loss. With that being said, the veteran has played just two games with Minnesota this season, so he's still getting situated in his reunion. He'll face an Atlanta defense that's ranked 26th in fantasy points allowed to QBs this campaign.

roster.name: James Cook III
roster.outlook: James Cook brings his usual heavy workload and a nine-game scoring streak into the Bills' challenging Week 12 matchup with the Chiefs. Cook collected 22 carries (on only 40 snaps) in Week 11 and is averaging 20.9 carries through 10 games. Despite a short turnaround to Thursday in Week 12, Cook's bell-cow role is secure, and he'll need that volume against a Kansas City front that's allowing just 3.5 yards per carry and six touchdowns.

roster.name: Nico Collins
roster.outlook: Nico Collins takes a three-game touchdown streak into Houston's Week 12 home game against the Ravens. He's still a weekly must-start option in most formats, but Collins has been more of a fantasy WR2 recently despite the strong play of Texans QB C.J. Stroud. Collins' usage has been inconsistent in Houston's deep WR room, as he has exceeded five targets only once in his last five appearances but was targeted 16 times in the outlier during that stretch. The reeling Ravens have lost six in a row, allowing 29.2 points per game over that span, but they have held WRs to just seven TDs all season. Baltimore is allowing a hefty 162 yards per game to the position, and the Texans' poor run blocking may not allow Houston to ride the ground game as the Ravens' recent opponents have.

roster.name: DeVonta Smith
roster.outlook: DeVonta Smith returned from injury for the Eagles and immediately received a heavy workload. Smith saw a team-high 12 targets in the 19-16 win. However, he managed just five catches for 41 yards for the game. Still, he retained his spot as the top target in the offense, and could find more success in Week 12 versus a porous Dallas Cowboys defense. "America's Team" has given up 21 passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 29th in the NFL. Dallas is also allowing 237.9 passing yards per tilt, which is 28th in the league.

roster.name: D'Andre Swift
roster.outlook: D'Andre Swift will aim to continue to lead Chicago's running game in Week 12 at Detroit. Swift remained the top running back in a Week 11 win over the Saints even with Kyle Monangai back from a turf toe injury. Swift's 15 touches easily outweighed Monangai's eight touches, but it wouldn't be crazy if the Bears ramped up the younger running back in the upcoming away matchup. Swift will look to build on a career-high 11 touchdowns versus a Lions defense that's ranked fifth in fantasy points allowed to running backs.

roster.name: Rome Odunze
roster.outlook: Rome Odunze will be a solid option in Chicago's passing offense again in Week 12 at Detroit. Odunze caught four targets for 45 yards in a Week 11 win over the Saints, increasing his four-catch streak to four games now. The third-year pass catcher has now pieced together a 36-573-1 receiving line on 55 targets this campaign. He'll now shift focus to a Lions defense that's ranked in the middle against fantasy WRs.

roster.name: Christian Watson
roster.outlook: Christian Watson will look to make a bang out of the bye week as the Packers play the Rams in Week 12. Watson struggled against a tough Minnesota defense in Week 10, catching three of five targets for a season-low 37 yards. The premier wideout has still impressed across the first 10 games of his fifth campaign, posting a 52-916-7 receiving line on 79 targets. His next challenge will be a Los Angeles defense that's ranked third in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.

roster.name: Justin Herbert
roster.outlook: Justin Herbert threw multiple touchdowns for the first time this season in the Chargers' Week 11 loss to the Jets, but he was placed in the concussion protocol after getting sacked six times. Both scores went to Ladd McConkey, but it was still an overall poor performance from Herbert, who failed to reach 200 passing yards for a third straight game. His 8:11 TD:INT ratio through 10 contests is awful, and an injury-ravaged offensive line has allowed Herbert to get sacked a league-high 39 times. If Herbert is cleared through the protocol in time, he'll face a Patriots defense in Week 12 that ranks 23rd in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs. If not, DJ Uiagalelei, who went undrafted out of Florida State in 2025, would likely get his first career NFL start.

roster.name: Travis Kelce
roster.outlook: Travis Kelce is coming off one of his best games of the season, catching six of seven targets for 74 yards and two touchdowns in Kansas City's Week 11 win over the Cardinals. The future Hall of Famer snapped a six-game TD drought with the performance, and with 586 receiving yards through 10 contests, he's still got a real shot at his first 1,000-yard campaign since 2022. Kelce is Patrick Mahomes' most reliable option, but he has plenty of competition for targets in a passing game that features plenty of depth but no clear No. 1 threat. Kelce will look to keep rolling in Week 12 against a Bills defense that ranks 11th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

roster.name: Matthew Golden
roster.outlook: Matthew Golden will look to shine against a tough Rams defense in Green Bay's Week 12 matchup out of the bye. Golden was the Packers' leading pass catcher in a Week 10 loss to Minnesota, hauling in five of nine targets for 70 yards. The second-year pass catcher has now recorded a 58-853-5 receiving line across 10 games, impressing after a subpar rookie season. He'll face a Los Angeles squad that's ranked third in fantasy points allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Eddy Pineiro
roster.outlook: Eddy Pineiro has been a PAT machine for the 49ers of late heading into a Week 12 matchup against Seattle. Pineiro didn't attempt a field goal in this past Sunday's win over Minnesota, but he made all five of his extra-point tries. It was the third straight game in which the veteran kicker has tried -- and converted -- five PATs, and he's gone just 2-for-2 on FG attempts in that span. San Francisco's offense has been so prolific at getting into the end zone that Pineiro's chances to kick field goals have been sparse, but the team will look to score any way it can against the Seahawks, who have given up the third-fewest points per game (17.5) this season.

roster.name: T.J. Hockenson
roster.outlook: T.J. Hockenson figures to be a top option in Minnesota's passing offense against the Falcons in Week 12. Hockenson was busy again in his return to the field against the 49ers in Week 11, catching six of seven targets for 55 yards. The veteran has now brought in four of more catches in each of his last four games. Atlanta has ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy TEs so far this season.

roster.name: Jonathan Taylor
roster.outlook: Jonathan Taylor has averaged just 16.3 touches over the Colts' last four games after averaging 22.4 touches in the first seven. Part of that decline has to do with the 3-8 Colts failing to remain competitive. Taylor has also started to cede a larger portion of rushing opportunities, including goal-line carries, to Seth McGowan, who won't suit up in Week 12 against the Giants due to a hamstring injury. Taylor remains too good to bench in most leagues, and perhaps Indianapolis' entire ground game will pick up the pace now that mobile, big-armed QB Anthony Richardson is running the show rather than Daniel Jones, but Taylor's nowhere near the top-five fantasy RB conversation at the moment. Treat the star RB as a fantasy RB2 for Week 12 against the Giants, who have been elite at defending the pass but rank in the middle of the pack against the run.

roster.name: Aaron Rodgers
roster.outlook: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers look to remain undefeated at home when they host the Broncos on Black Friday in Week 12. He threw for 227 yards (30-of-44) with one TD and no INTs and rushed five times for 29 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 11 loss. The production was the most for Rodgers since he put up 253 passing yards in Week 6, as the Steelers' offense continued to underwhelm in a second straight defeat. The 42-year-old signal-caller will attempt to be more effective versus a Denver defense allowing 22.0 fantasy points per game (T-24th) to opposing QBs.

roster.name: Malik Nabers
roster.outlook: Malik Nabers snagged a touchdown pass for the Giants last game. Nabers finished the win over the Jags with seven catches for 55 yards and his third score of the season. Nabers was targeted 12 times, the third time in 2026 he received double-digit targets. In Week 12, the Giants will face a Colts defense allowing 220.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 14th in the NFL. However, Indy has also surrendered 20 throwing scores, which is 28th in the league.

roster.name: Cam Skattebo
roster.outlook: Cam Skattebo fumbled yet again for the Giants last game. The turnover ultimately did not cost his team the win this time, though Skattebo managed just 34 yards on 14 carries overall versus a stout Jacksonville run defense. If Skattebo can hold onto the ball, he should have better luck against the Colts in Week 12. Indianapolis is allowing 134.4 rushing yards per tilt, which is 29th in the NFL.

roster.name: Bucky Irving
roster.outlook: Bucky Irving is expected to remain one of fantasy's top running backs during the Buccaneers' Week 12 matchup against the Panthers. Irving was one of Tampa Bay's few bright spots during the Week 11 loss to the Lions, accounting for 100 scrimmage yards and one touchdown on 21 touches. He ranks sixth in the NFL in touches (21.0) and ninth in scrimmage yards (103.1) per game, which bodes well for his fantasy look going forward. Additionally, he's in for a very favorable Week 12 matchup against a Carolina defense that's allowed 28.6 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season, the most in the NFL.

roster.name: Tucker Kraft
roster.outlook: Tucker Kraft will aim to get back on track as the Packers play the Rams in Week 12. Kraft entered Green Bay's bye with back-to-back one-catch games, which was even more disappointing given he looked to finally be getting on track prior. The fourth-year tight end has now sported a 37-370-3 receiving line over 10 outings this campaign. Los Angeles has also ceded the fewest fantasy points per game to TEs.

roster.name: Trevor Lawrence
roster.outlook: Trevor Lawrence was held to a 1:2 TD:INT ratio in Jacksonville's Week 11 road loss to the Giants, but he has been sensational at home, with a 10:1 TD:INT ratio in three games at EverBank Stadium. He's a set-and-forget fantasy starter for Week 12 with No. 1 overall QB upside against Tennessee's generous secondary. The Titans have allowed 12 touchdown passes over their last three games, three of which were thrown by Lawrence in Jacksonville's 40-23 Week 10 win at Tennessee. Lawrence should have little trouble carving up Tennessee's secondary like a Thanksgiving turkey as long as the game stays competitive; however, Jacksonville's high-powered offense could throttle down late if the heavily favored Jaguars build a comfortable lead.

roster.name: Jordan Mason
roster.outlook: Jordan Mason will aim to make the most of his usage as the Vikings play the Falcons in Week 12. Mason rushed the ball 11 times for 38 yards and logged one catch for minus-1 yard in a Week 11 loss to the 49ers. He's now been unable to find the end zone since returning from injury in Week 7, and his receiving work has yet to make up for otherwise subpar rushing totals. Luckily, Atlanta has ranked 28th in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.

roster.name: Braelon Allen
roster.outlook: Braelon Allen may garner enough work in the Jets' Week 12 matchup with the Dolphins to be viable. Despite Breece Hall's return to health, Allen has at least eight carries in three straight games, with the Jets being run-centric. He found ample holes in the Dolphins' front as a lead back in Week 7 and can repeat that per-touch success, worthy of flex consideration.

roster.name: Ollie Gordon II
roster.outlook: Ollie Gordon will look to repeat prior success when the Dolphins face the Jets for the second time this year in Week 12. He drew only 11 carries in Week 11, his lowest total since Week 4, but burst through for 6.3 yards per carry, also his best mark since Week 4. Gordon rushed for 103 yards on 25 carries against the Jets in Week 7. Their defense has allowed 4.6 yards per carry and eight rushing scores through 11 games, surrendering an additional four touchdown receptions, and Gordon is more involved in the passing game with McCord under center.

roster.name: Jaylen Warren
roster.outlook: In Week 12, Jaylen Warren and the Steelers aim to snap a two-game losing streak when they host the Broncos on Black Friday. He had nine carries for 28 yards and caught two of three targets for one yard during Pittsburgh's Week 11 loss. Warren got 11 touches compared to nine for backfield mate Rico Dowdle, but it was an overall quiet outing for both. The Steelers have shifted to more of a timeshare with Dowdle now fully healthy, leaving Warren as a TD-or-bust option versus Denver's 25th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (24.9) to RBs.

roster.name: Chuba Hubbard
roster.outlook: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain the focal point of the Panthers' offense in the Week 12 matchup against the Buccaneers. Hubbard has now received 59 touches over his last two games, accounting for 292 total yards (212 rushing and 80 receiving) and four touchdowns. He ranks fifth in the NFL in touches per game (21.9) and seventh in scrimmage yards per game (107.8), likely remaining one of fantasy's top running backs for the remainder of the season. Hubbard is in for a very difficult Week 12 matchup, however, as Tampa Bay's defense has allowed the fewest fantasy points per game to opposing running backs (17.2) in the league this season.

roster.name: Zay Flowers
roster.outlook: Zay Flowers and Baltimore travel to square off against the Texans in Week 12. He caught eight of 11 targets for 97 yards and rushed once for minus-13 yards during Baltimore's Week 11 loss. Flowers led his team in receptions, yardage and targets, but it was Rashod Bateman who was on the receiving end of Jacoby Brissett's 52-yard TD pass. Flowers' fantasy stock is on the rise with Brissett under center, and they'll face a favorable matchup against Houston's 27th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (35.7) to WRs.

roster.name: Spencer Shrader
roster.outlook: Spencer Shrader's stellar start is a distant memory. The struggling kicker has gone just 6-for-10 on field-goal attempts over the past five games after making all 18 of his attempts through Week 6. Indianapolis has switched QBs from Daniel Jones to Anthony Richardson after dropping six of its last seven games, but moving the ball will likely remain difficult for the Colts' underwhelming offense in Week 12 against the Giants, who allow the seventh-fewest scrimmage yards (310.5) and 12th-fewest points (21.4) per game. Shrader is a risky Week 12 fantasy option.

roster.name: Dalton Kincaid
roster.outlook: Dalton Kincaid will need to overcome thumb and ankle injuries if he's to help the Bills in a promising Week 12 matchup with the Chiefs. His playing time and production have slid over the last three weeks coming out of Buffalo's Week 7 bye. Kincaid's snap share has dropped to around 50%, ceding his slot role to Dawson Knox, who is serving as an additional blocker on the line. If Kincaid plays, opportunities await, with Kansas City allowing tight ends to catch at least four passes in three straight games and five overall touchdowns. They have also yielded the seventh-most fantasy points per game to the position.

roster.name: Brenton Strange
roster.outlook: Brenton Strange is a viable low-end starter at TE in Week 12 against the Titans, though Jacksonville's wideouts are more likely to find success versus Tennessee's leaky secondary. One of Strange's two TDs this season came in Week 10 at Tennessee, but he had a season-low nine receiving yards in that game. The Titans are holding TEs to 42 yards per game, though they have given up six TDs to the position. Strange ranks 14th at his position with 38 receiving yards per game.

roster.name: Jahmyr Gibbs
roster.outlook: Jahmyr Gibbs will look to keep his tear going in Week 12 as Detroit faces Chicago on Thanksgiving. Gibbs eventually broke down an otherwise stingy Tampa Bay run defense in Week 11, rushing 23 times for 98 yards and two touchdowns and catching four passes for 20 yards. The superstar has now surpassed 95 rushing yards in seven of 10 games this season, and he's totaled 13 scores on the ground. He'll face a Bears defense that's ranked relatively middle-of-the-pack versus fantasy RBs this season, and that Travis Etienne averaged 5.42 yards per carry against this past Sunday.

roster.name: A.J. Brown
roster.outlook: A.J. Brown seems unlikely to play in Week 12 when the Patriots face the Chargers due to lingering hamstring issues. Mack Hollins, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams could see elevated roles, but with Tommy DeVito under center, all will be volatile options.

roster.name: Ladd McConkey
roster.outlook: Ladd McConkey made his mark in the red zone during the Chargers' Week 11 loss to the Jets, catching five of eight targets for 37 yards and two touchdowns. The third-year wide receiver hadn't found the end zone since Week 1 as he endures an injury-plagued season, but when he's been in the lineup, he's been Justin Herbert's clear top option. Unfortunately, it could be Herbert's turn on the sideline, as the quarterback was diagnosed with a concussion after the loss to the Jets. McConkey's outlook would get a big downgrade if DJ Uiagalelei is under center for his first career NFL start, but regardless of who is throwing him the ball, he'll be facing a Patriots secondary that ranks an enticing 31st in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Joe Burrow
roster.outlook: In Week 12, Joe Burrow and the Bengals host the Saints in an interconference clash. He completed 28 of 40 pass attempts for 300 yards with two TDs and zero INTs while rushing twice for minus-one yard during Cincinnati's Week 11 loss. Burrow delivered his fourth 300-yard outing of the season while extending his streak of games without an interception to three. He'll look to get his team back in the win column versus a New Orleans defense allowing 19.8 fantasy points per game (T-11th) to QBs.

roster.name: DK Metcalf
roster.outlook: In Week 12, DK Metcalf and the Steelers look to stay undefeated at home when they battle the Broncos on Black Friday. He caught one of four targets for two yards before being ejected in the third quarter of Pittsburgh's Week 11 loss. Metcalf's season continues to spiral out of control, and luckily for him, the veteran receiver will not face a suspension from the league following the scuffle. Metcalf will be on the field versus Denver, but he should remain on fantasy benches.

roster.name: Cameron Dicker
roster.outlook: Cameron Dicker hasn't missed a kick since Week 3, going 16-for-16 on field goal attempts and 10-for-10 on PATs over the last seven games. The Chargers' struggling offense hasn't provided him with consistent opportunities, but Dicker's reliability provides him with a solid floor. With Justin Herbert in the concussion protocol, DJ Uiagalelei could be in line to make his first career NFL start at quarterback, adding a lot more uncertainty to the picture. Even if Herbert plays, Dicker will be a volatile option at kicker in Week 12 against a Patriots team allowing 24.2 points per game, 19th in the league.

roster.name: Brock Purdy
roster.outlook: Brock Purdy will face another tough defense when the 49ers host Seattle in Week 12. The star quarterback solved Minnesota's previously stingy defense this past Sunday in a 35-10 victory in Mexico City, throwing for 255 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions. Purdy and San Francisco's offense seems to be firing on all cylinders right now, especially after the return of All-Pro wideout Mike Evans. Still, the Seahawks could present a stiffer test than most, as they have yielded the fewest fantasy points per game (14.1) to quarterbacks and held Purdy to a season-low 189 passing yards in their first meeting Week 5.

roster.name: Deebo Samuel Sr.
roster.outlook: Deebo Samuel continues to be a Swiss Army knife for San Francisco heading into a Week 12 tilt against the Seahawks. In this past Sunday's win over the Vikings, Samuel recorded two carries for 27 yards, caught three of four targets for 20 yards and returned two kickoffs for 57 yards. While that might not add up to substantial fantasy production, Samuel's skill set could be invaluable for the 49ers against a tough defense like the Seahawks'. Seattle has given up the fewest yards per target (5.89) to wideouts this season, so San Francisco may look to be creative in order to push the ball downfield.

roster.name: Amon-Ra St. Brown
roster.outlook: Amon-Ra St. Brown will look to keep his touchdown streak alive as the Lions play the Bears in Week 12. St. Brown punched in another score in a Week 11 win over the Buccaneers, which made up for his otherwise mediocre five catches for 37 yards. He's now brought in 70 of 97 targets for 792 yards and eight touchdowns this campaign. Chicago has ranked a tough 10th in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.

roster.name: Harold Fannin Jr.
roster.outlook: In Week 12, Harold Fannin Jr. and the Browns look to go 5-0 at home when the Raiders visit on Sunday Night Football. He caught seven of nine targets for 91 yards during Cleveland's Week 10 victory. Fannin paced his team in every receiving category, finishing as the leader in yardage for the second time in three games. Over his last four outings, he's registered a 25-378-1 line on 32 targets. Fannin will look to stay hot against a Las Vegas defense allowing 16.7 fantasy points per game (28th) to TEs.

roster.name: Chig Okonkwo
roster.outlook: Chig Okonkwo continues to serve as an excellent safety valve for the Commanders. Okonkwo reeled in four passes for 66 yards in the stunning 22-20 win over the Bengals. Okonkwo has at least four catches in five of his last six games played, though he is still looking for his first touchdown of the season. In Week 12, Chig will face a lackluster Arizona pass defense. The Cardinals are allowing 226.4 passing yards per tilt, which is 20th in the NFL. In addition, the Cardinals have surrendered the most passing touchdowns in the league to date.

roster.name: Travis Etienne Jr.
roster.outlook: Travis Etienne is expected to remain the Saints' top rusher during the Week 12 matchup against the Bengals. In his two games since returning from a hamstring injury, Etienne has accumulated 90 rushing yards (4.1 yards per carry) and 20 receiving yards without finding the end zone. Despite his lack of production, Etienne was received 14 of the Saints' 16 running back carries during the Week 11 loss to the Bears, suggesting he's got a firm hold on the No. 1 role. Etienne is also in for an unfavorable matchup, as Cincinnati has allowed just 20.8 points per game to opposing running backs this season.

roster.name: Kyren Williams
roster.outlook: Kyren Williams has been dealing with a sore toe but is expected to play in the Rams' Week 12 matchup versus Green Bay. Williams logged a season-low 32 total yards (23 rushing, nine receiving) versus Arizona his last time out, so he'll be looking for a big bounce-back performance against the Packers. With that said, Blake Corum -- who went off for a season-best 119 yards and scored a touchdown in that game against the Cardinals -- continues to get double-digit touches every week, denting Williams' ceiling to an extent. Both backs could find success against a Green Bay defense that has given up 12 rushing TDs to running backs, tied for fourth-most in the league.

roster.name: Bijan Robinson
roster.outlook: Bijan Robinson is expected to remain the focal point of Atlanta's offense during the Week 12 matchup against the Vikings. Robinson has been one of fantasy's most productive running backs this season, ranking fourth in the NFL in scrimmage yards (120.7) and touches (22.0) per game. Despite the Falcons' recent offensive struggles, Robinson has continued to be impactful for fantasy purposes, averaging 17.3 points per game over the team's last three games. However, he could struggle against a strong Vikings defense that's allowed just 18.7 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this season.

roster.name: Josh Allen
roster.outlook: Josh Allen will look to steal the spotlight in a marquee Week 12 Thursday matchup when the Bills face the Chiefs. Allen is coming off a curious outing in Week 11 against the Dolphins, throwing a season-high 45 times while not attempting a rush and tossing a season-high two interceptions. Kansas City has allowed the third-fewest fantasy points per game to quarterbacks, with just eight touchdown passes and no rushing scores through 10 games. Allen is a touch more vulnerable than his typical elite status.

roster.name: Kenneth Walker III
roster.outlook: Kenneth Walker has missed Kansas City's last two games with a groin injury, and in his absence, rookie Emmett Johnson has dazzled. Walker is in no danger of losing his hold on the No. 1 job in the backfield given his own outstanding start to the season, but Johnson's performance could lead to more of a timeshare as Andy Reid keeps one eye on the health of his roster ahead of the playoffs. If Walker is cleared to return for Week 12's Thursday Night Football clash with the Bills, he'll take on a defense that ranks 21st in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

roster.name: Emeka Egbuka
roster.outlook: Emeka Egbuka is expected to remain the Buccaneers' top wideout during the Week 12 matchup against the Panthers, Egbuka was relatively quiet during the Week 11 loss to the Lions, catching two of five targets for 18 yards. The second-year wideout has struggled to find his footing since returning from injury in the Week 9 loss to the Bears, catching just five of 10 targets for 56 yards in two contests. Despite this, he's expected to remain the team's top receiving option against a Carolina defense that's allowed 31.9 fantasy points per game to opposing WR groups this season.

roster.name: DJ Moore
roster.outlook: DJ Moore will try to maintain his recent scoring spree when the Bills face a strong Chiefs secondary in Week 12. Moore tied a season-high with 10 targets in Week 11, recording at least 82 yards receiving and scoring for the second time in as many games and third in four outings. Kansas City counters with only three touchdowns allowed to receivers in 10 contests, and a mere 6.6 yards per target. Moore will need steady volume to finish in the upper tier of receivers.

roster.name: Luther Burden III
roster.outlook: Luther Burden will look to bounce back as the Bears play the Lions in Week 12. Burden posted a season-worst performance in Week 11 against the Saints, hauling in two of three targets for just 10 yards. Either way, he's posted a career-best 51-654-4 receiving line across just 10 games this season. He'll face a Detroit defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack versus fantasy WRs this campaign.

roster.name: Kyle Pitts Sr.
roster.outlook: Kyle Pitts is expected to remain one of Atlanta's top pass catchers during the Week 12 matchup against the Vikings. Pitts has been relatively inconsistent this year, catching 29 of 42 targets for 270 yards and four touchdowns. He's tallied fewer than 10 fantasy points in seven of 10 games this season, making him hard to trust as a weekly fantasy starter. This is especially true due to a difficult matchup in Week 12, as Minnesota's defense has allowed just 9.9 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season, the best mark in the NFL.

roster.name: Courtland Sutton
roster.outlook: Courtland Sutton disappeared from the game plan in the Broncos' Week 11 win over the Raiders, failing to catch either of his two targets. It's the first time since Week 7 of the 2024 season he hasn't caught a pass, but with the offense leaning more heavily on rookie running back Jonah Coleman, there hasn't been much need for Bo Nix to air it out. Sutton is on pace to fall short of 500 receiving yards over a full season for the first time in his career, and fail to reach 50 catches for the first time since he was a rookie in 2018. He'll be a risky play in Week 12 against a Steelers secondary that ranks 12th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Kyle Monangai
roster.outlook: Kyle Monangai will look to get more opportunities as the Bears play the Lions in Week 12. Monangai was quiet in his return from a five-game absence due to turf toe, carrying the ball eight times for just 18 yards. The second-year ball carrier could be in line for a ramped up role in the upcoming away matchup, but D'Andre Swift currently looks to have the RB1 role in his grasp. Detroit's defense has ranked fifth in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.

roster.name: Alvin Kamara
roster.outlook: Alvin Kamara will likely play a minimal offensive role during the Saints' Week 12 matchup against the Bengals. Despite finding the end zone during the Week 11 loss to the Saints, Kamara played just eight offensive snaps while Travis Etienne and CJ Donaldson each played 32. Additionally, Kamara has received just seven touches over the Saints' last two games, suggesting his role in the offense has diminished. Expect Kamara to have minimal value in Week 12 against a Bengals defense that's given up just 294 receiving yards to RBs through nine games this year.

roster.name: Tre Tucker
roster.outlook: Tre Tucker has yet to get on the same page as new starting quarterback Fernando Mendoza. Tucker recorded 10 targets in the Raiders' Week 11 loss to the Broncos, but he was able to haul in just two for 50 yards. Meanwhile, Jack Bech posted an 8-88-1 line on nine targets, and he may be making a push to replace Tucker as the team's No. 1 wide receiver. Tucker will attempt to prove he deserves to continue seeing high volume from Mendoza in Week 12 against a Browns secondary that ranks 14th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Tyler Bass
roster.outlook: Tyler Bass continues to thrive in the Bills' potent offense ahead of a Week 12 matchup with the Chiefs. He converted four of five field goal attempts and two extra points in Week 11, his fifth game in his last six with at least three field goals. While the Chiefs have allowed only 12 PATs in 10 games, they've surrendered 22 field goals, and with Buffalo likely to test that defense more than other opponents, Bass should again earn enough scoring chances to merit heavy fantasy consideration.

roster.name: Darren Waller
roster.outlook: Darren Waller is expected to remain the Panthers' top pass-catching tight end during the Week 12 matchup against the Buccaneers. Despite being overshadowed by Mitchell Evans (5-44-1) during the Week 11 win over the Ravens, Waller remains first amongst Panthers tight ends in targets (41), receptions (28) and yards (365). In his first game against the Buccaneers this season, Waller was targeted just twice but caught a 50-yard touchdown to salvage his fantasy day. He could thrive in Week 12, as Tampa Bay's defense has given up 15.0 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.

roster.name: Ja'Marr Chase
roster.outlook: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals look to get back in the win column when they host the 3-7 Saints in Week 12. He was shockingly quiet during Cincinnati's Week 11 loss, catching five of nine targets for 31 yards. Chase's streak of consecutive games with either a touchdown or 100+ receiving yards ended at five. The rainy weather didn't stop the Bengals from throwing, as Joe Burrow attempted 40 passes, but the superstar duo was unable to establish much of a connection. Chase will attempt to bounce back versus a New Orleans secondary allowing 28.6 fantasy points per game (8th) to opposing WRs.

roster.name: Drake London
roster.outlook: Drake London is expected to remain the Falcons' top wideout during the Week 12 matchup against the Vikings. Prior to Atlanta's Week 11 bye, London had one of his best performances of the 2026 season, catching six of 12 targets for 109 yards. With Michael Penix at quarterback this year, London has averaged 5.5 receptions and 90.1 receiving yards per game, making him one of the league's most productive receivers. Despite this, London could definitely struggle against the Vikings in Week 12, as they have allowed just 27.8 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this year.

roster.name: Breece Hall
roster.outlook: Breece Hall is slated for a heavy workload for the Jets' run-first offense entering an inviting matchup against the Dolphins in Week 12. Hall amassed 20 rushes in Week 11, adding three catches, and has now topped 100 total yards in consecutive outings. Miami is allowing a modest 4.3 yards per carry but 11 total touchdowns (six rushing, five receiving) to running backs. Braelon Allen excelled against the Dolphins in Hall's absence earlier in the season, so Hall should produce in Week 12, even if ceding some carries to Allen. Hall remains a must-start.

roster.name: Quinshon Judkins
roster.outlook: In Week 12, Quinshon Judkins and the Browns welcome the Raiders to town on Sunday Night Football. He had 10 carries for 38 yards and a touchdown and caught three of five targets for 33 yards during Cleveland's Week 10 win. Judkins has struggled to find running room in 2026, rushing 126 times for 423 yards (3.4 YPC) and four scores, but there's hope that could change in Week 12. Las Vegas allows 26.9 fantasy points per game (28th) to RBs and just gave up 133 yards and three TDs on the ground in their latest outing.

roster.name: David Montgomery
roster.outlook: David Montgomery rushed for a season-high 107 yards in Week 11 against the Colts, successfully returning to action from a groin injury that had sidelined him since Week 5. Montgomery handled 29 touches in a workhorse role due to the absence of Woody Marks (concussion), who has a chance to return in Week 12 against the Ravens. If Marks plays, both Houston RBs would be solid flex plays, likely working in a timeshare. Should Marks sit again, Montgomery would be a high-end RB2 with another heavy workload anticipated against a Ravens run defense that allowed Omarion Hampton and Chuba Hubbard to rush for a combined 225 yards and three TDs over the past two games. Montgomery is averaging a meager 3.1 yards per carry, so he relies on volume and scoring opportunities to counteract his poor efficiency.

roster.name: Carnell Tate
roster.outlook: Carnell Tate got into his first game action since Week 7 and scored a 59-yard touchdown in his return from a shoulder injury in Week 11 against the Cowboys. His other four targets went for a combined minus-1 yard, and Tate finished third on the Titans in both receiving yards and targets, trailing Chimere Dike and Calvin Ridley. Tate continues to have the highest ceiling among Tennessee's pass catchers, and the team's entire offense has been trending up lately, even though that improvement hasn't translated to wins heading into a Week 12 trip to Jacksonville. This will be Tate's first encounter with a Jaguars defense that's allowing 162 yards per game to WRs but has held the position to five TDs, as he missed the Week 10 meeting between these AFC South rivals. The rookie, fourth overall pick is a solid fantasy WR3 or flex option.

roster.name: Sam LaPorta
roster.outlook: Sam LaPorta will look to build off a bounce-back showing as the Lions play the Bears in Week 12. LaPorta hauled in three of six targets for 62 yards in a Week 11 win over Tampa Bay, with most of his output coming from a 47-yard catch early in the game. Still, this receiving line included his best yardage total since before Detroit's bye in Week 5, so he'll hopefully be able to build on it in the weeks to come. He'll face a Chicago defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy tight ends in the last four weeks.

roster.name: Josh Jacobs
roster.outlook: Josh Jacobs will look to make a return as the Packers play the Rams in Week 12. Jacobs missed Week 10 against Minnesota with a finger injury, and while he's had a week off to get back to full health, he was unable to practice fully on Monday. If the veteran ball carrier is good to go, he'll look to come out on top of a crowded backfield against a Los Angeles defense that's ranked third in fantasy points allowed to RBs.

roster.name: Woody Marks
roster.outlook: Woody Marks missed Houston's Week 11 win over the Colts due to a concussion. If he clears protocol in time to face the Ravens in Week 12, Marks would be a decent flex option while splitting carries with David Montgomery, who returned from a groin injury in Week 11. Marks has exceeded 40 scrimmage yards only once in five games alongside Montgomery, and that was a game in which Montgomery exited early due to an injury, but Houston's entire RB room should benefit from facing a reeling Ravens defense that has allowed multiple rushing touchdowns in four consecutive games. Baltimore is giving up 29.2 points per game during its current six-game losing streak.

roster.name: Jared Goff
roster.outlook: Jared Goff will look to keep Detroit rolling in Week 12 against the Bears. Goff put together another solid performance in a Week 11 win over the Buccaneers, slinging for 278 yards and two touchdowns. The veteran now sports a 20:4 TD:INT and has thrown for 2,716 yards across 10 games. He'll face a Chicago defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack versus fantasy quarterbacks so far this year and allowed 222 passing yards, one touchdown and one interception to Tyler Shough this past Sunday.

roster.name: Jordan Love
roster.outlook: Jordan Love will travel to take on the Rams in a Week 12 matchup for Green Bay out of the bye. Love and the Packers went into their off week with many questions, with the starting quarterback throwing for 220 yards and a 1:1 TD:INT versus Minnesota in Week 10. Love has still put together an impressive first half of the season, with multiple touchdowns in all but one game and 2,838 passing yards across 10 weeks. Los Angeles has ranked a tough fourth in fantasy points allowed to QBs this campaign, so Love might have his work cut out for him to return to dominance.

roster.name: Blake Corum
roster.outlook: Blake Corum will look to build on a season-best performance when the Rams host the Packers in Week 12. Corum rumbled for a season-high 100 rushing yards and a touchdown in Week 10 against Arizona while adding three catches for 19 yards. He should be fresh with Los Angeles having been on bye in Week 12, and Corum could be even more important than usual if backfield mate Kyren Williams' sore toe inhibits him at all. Both ball carriers could be productive against a Green Bay defense that ranks 26th in the NFL with 21.1 fantasy points per game allowed to RBs this season.

roster.name: Cam Little
roster.outlook: Cam Little has come up big for fantasy managers recently with three consecutive 4-for-4 performances on field-goal attempts. He's in great position to keep rolling in a Week 12 home game against the Titans, who have surrendered a whopping 44.7 points per game in their last three. That woeful stretch from Tennessee's defense includes Jacksonville's 40-23 win in Week 10, during which Little converted all four of his PAT tries to go with four field goals. Little's a set-and-forget Week 12 fantasy starter.

roster.name: Jordyn Tyson
roster.outlook: Jordyn Tyson will look to bounce back from a rough performance during the Saints' Week 12 matchup against the Bengals. After catching 11 of 13 targets for 80 yards during the Week 10 loss to the Panthers, Tyson was a non-factor in Week 11, logging one reception for six yards. He remains firmly behind Chris Olave in the team's WR corps but could still be valuable for fantasy purposes, with quarterback Tyler Shough averaging the second-most pass attempts per game (38.5) in the NFL. Tyson could struggle in Week 12, however, with Cincinnati's secondary allowing just 7.5 yards per target to opposing wideouts this year.

roster.name: CeeDee Lamb
roster.outlook: CeeDee Lamb crossed the 100-yard threshold yet again for the Cowboys last game. Lamb caught 11 passes for 132 yards and a touchdown in the 51-30 dismantling of the Titans. Lamb has scored in three-straight contests, and has gone over the 100-yard receiving mark in two of those outings. He is second in the NFL in receiving yardage overall, and first in receptions. In Week 12, the Cowboys will face a mediocre Eagles pass defense. Philadelphia is allowing 222.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 17th in the NFL. However, the Eagles have only given up 14 passing touchdowns, which is tied for ninth in the league.

roster.name: Justin Jefferson
roster.outlook: Justin Jefferson will look to get back in the end zone as the Vikings play the Falcons in Week 12. Jefferson has benefited greatly from the reintroduction of Kirk Cousins in the last two weeks, totaling 16 catches for 142 yards in that stretch. The star pass catcher has now put together a 47-553-4 receiving line over nine games, which could be greatly improved in the coming weeks if he keeps a strong connection with Cousins. He'll shift his attention to an Atlanta defense that's ranked 25th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Garrett Wilson
roster.outlook: Garrett Wilson brings inconsistent volume into the Jets' Week 12 matchup with the Dolphins. Wilson drew only five targets in Week 11, with the Jets attempting only 21 passes, and quarterback Geno Smith has not completed 20 passes for three straight outings. Wilson has four games with double-digit targets and four games with 44 receiving yards or fewer through 10 games. With the Jets likely to remain run-first, Wilson's workload could be limited facing a secondary that's allowing a whopping 9.2 yards per target but the fourth-fewest fantasy points per game to receivers due to limited volume.

roster.name: Javonte Williams
roster.outlook: Javonte Williams scored twice last game for the Cowboys.  Williams rushed 18 times for 67 yards and one touchdown on the ground, while also catching three passes for 24 yards and a second score during the 51-30 blowout of the Titans. Williams has 12 combined touchdowns through 11 contests for Dallas. In Week 12, he will face an Eagles defense allowing 120.8 rushing yards per tilt, which is 21st in the NFL.  Likewise, Philadelphia has surrendered 10 rushing scores this season, which is tied for 18th in the league.

roster.name: Bhayshul Tuten
roster.outlook: Bhayshul Tuten aggravated an ankle injury in Jacksonville's previous game. However, he reportedly avoided a serious injury and could still suit up in Week 12 against the Titans. The 2025 fourth-round pick hasn't missed a game during his second NFL year, though Tuten had a season-low 29 yards in Week 9 while playing through this ankle injury and just posted his second-lowest total of the season with 53 scrimmage yards in Week 11. If Tuten gets the green light, he can be plugged in as a fantasy RB2 against a Titans defense that's allowing 133 scrimmage yards per game to RBs, despite his injury concerns. Should Tuten sit, Chris Rodriguez would be in line to lead Jacksonville's ground game, while LeQuint Allen and Ameer Abdullah offer receiving upside out of the backfield.

roster.name: Tyler Warren
roster.outlook: Tyler Warren has been held to just three catches in two games since the Colts traded starting WRs Josh Downs and Keenan Allen. Rather than collecting even more targets as the team's top remaining pass catcher, Warren has struggled to create separation as defenses have focused on stopping him. Warren can't sink much lower following the Colts' QB change from Daniel Jones to Anthony Richardson, even though Richardson's 15-game sample as an NFL starter suggests he's more likely to air it out deep to wide receivers or take off running than find his TE on a short or intermediate route. Week 12 against the Giants will mark the first time that Warren, a 2025 first-round pick, and Richardson, a 2023 first-round pick, start in the same game. Benching Warren is justifiable if you have a solid alternative, but leaving him in and hoping for a spark with Richardson is defensible.

roster.name: Dak Prescott
roster.outlook: Dak Prescott scored five touchdowns for the second-straight game for the Cowboys. Prescott threw for 325 yards and four touchdowns, while rushing for another score in the 51-30 thrashing of the Titans. Prescott has thrown for over 300 yards in three-straight contests, and now has 25 passing touchdowns on the season. That places him second in the NFL behind Joe Burrow. In Week 12, the Cowboys will face a mediocre Eagles pass defense. Philadelphia is allowing 222.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 17th in the NFL. However, the Eagles have only given up 14 passing touchdowns, which is tied for ninth in the league.

roster.name: Mike Evans
roster.outlook: Mike Evans will look to move further past his Achilles injury when the 49ers host Seattle in Week 12. Evans returned from a three-game absence this past Sunday against Minnesota and posted a 6-109-1 receiving line on seven targets. The veteran wideout did log just a 42% offensive snap share, so San Francisco may have been easing him back in workload-wise despite his big stat line. Evans could find the sledding tougher against the Seahawks, who have allowed the fewest fantasy points per game (12.8) to wideouts this season, though Evans burned Seattle for a 7-113-1 receiving line in their first meeting this season.

roster.name: Caleb Williams
roster.outlook: Caleb Williams will look to lead a more efficient Chicago offense in Week 12 at Detroit. Williams put together a passable stat line in a Week 11 win over the Saints, but the Bears offense looked sluggish in the matchup. The third-year quarterback has dished out two touchdowns in three of his last four games and thrown for 240 or more yards in all but one of his last five. He'll face a Lions defense that's ranked a favorable 31st in fantasy points allowed to quarterbacks this season.

roster.name: Chris Godwin Jr.
roster.outlook: Chris Godwin is expected to remain the Buccaneers' top safety blanket during the Week 12 matchup against the Panthers. Godwin has underwhelmed over Tampa Bay's last three contests, catching just five of seven targets for 29 yards. Despite ranking second on the team in receptions (32) this season, Godwin likely doesn't carry much fantasy value without finding the end zone. He could have plenty of opportunities against Carolina in Week 12, however, as the Panthers' secondary has allowed 12.6 receptions per game to opposing wideouts this season.

roster.name: Jordan Addison
roster.outlook: Jordan Addison is unlikely to play in Week 12 as the Vikings take on Atlanta. Addison is set to sit out another week after undergoing thumb surgery, so he'll aim to get back to full health for Week 13 against Carolina. He's sported a quiet 18-277-1 receiving line over seven games this campaign. Addison's absence should continue to boost Jauan Jennings and Tai Felton's playing time.

roster.name: Mark Andrews
roster.outlook: In Week 12, Mark Andrews and the Ravens are back on the road to battle the Texans. He brought in two of three targets for 14 yards during Baltimore's loss in Week 11. Andrews' follow-up to his season-best performance in Week 10 was disappointing, especially when considering Jacoby Brissett attempted 37 passes and the Ravens scored 33 points. Next up for Andrews is a Houston defense allowing 10.0 fantasy points per game to TEs, the second-lowest mark in the league.

roster.name: Ka'imi Fairbairn
roster.outlook: Ka'imi Fairbairn has missed just one of his 48 kicks this season, going 20-for-21 on field-goal attempts and 27-for-27 on PAT tries. Houston's excellent kicker should get plenty of opportunities at home in Week 12 against the Ravens, who are giving up 26.7 points per game overall and 32.4 points per game over their last five, all of which Baltimore lost. Fairbairn is a set-and-forget fantasy starter in this appetizing matchup.

roster.name: Jakobi Meyers
roster.outlook: Jakobi Meyers has drawn at least six targets in four of Jacksonville's last five games, reaching 10 targets twice over that span. His decent volume as the Jaguars' No. 2 WR makes Meyers an appealing Week 12 flex option against Tennessee's league-worst secondary, which is allowing an average of 16 catches for 210 yards per game to wide receivers. Meyers turned six targets into just three catches for 34 yards in Week 10 at Tennessee, but he's capable of producing a more impressive stat line in this home rematch as he tries to snap a TD drought that dates back to Week 3.

roster.name: Ashton Jeanty
roster.outlook: Ashton Jeanty finally had a breakout performance in the Raiders' Week 11 loss to the Broncos. The second-year running back gained 79 yards on the ground on just 11 carries, while adding a 5-90-1 line on eight targets. With the Las Vegas offense looking like it will stay effective with rookie Fernando Mendoza at quarterback, Jeanty should get more opportunities to establish himself as a three-down threat, but his primary strength still appears to be as a pass catcher, and he leads all RBs this season in targets, catches and receiving yards. In Week 12, Jeanty will take aim at a Browns defense that has been among the stingiest in the NFL in receiving production allowed to backs, but which ranks 12th in fantasy points per game allowed to the position.

roster.name: Trey McBride
roster.outlook: Trey McBride stands as perhaps the Cardinals' last healthy reliable producer ahead of a battle against the Commanders in Week 12. With WR Michael Wilson (neck) done for the season and RB Jeremiyah Love (ankle) still on IR, McBride has been counted on to carry the offense. The star tight end has mostly held up, including in a loss to Kansas City this past Sunday when he posted a 9-54-0 line on a team-high 14 targets. It remains to be seen if McBride will be catching passes from rookie Carson Beck (back) or veteran journeyman Josh Johnson this weekend, but either way he'll likely be the team's offensive focus in a matchup versus a Washington defense that has allowed the second-most fantasy points per game (13.5) to tight ends this season.

roster.name: Tetairoa McMillan
roster.outlook: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain the Panthers' top wideout during the Week 12 matchup against the Buccaneers. McMillan had a nice bounce-back performance in the Week 11 win over the Ravens, catching six of nine targets for 71 yards and a score. The second-year pro is averaging team-highs in targets (8.7), receptions (5.5) and receiving yards per game (73.1), which bodes well for his fantasy outlook going forward. McMillan is in for a tough Week 12 matchup, however, as the Buccaneers' defense has allowed just 30.4 fantasy points per game to opposing wide-receiver rooms this year.

roster.name: Tee Higgins
roster.outlook: Tee Higgins and the Bengals return home for an interconference clash against the Saints in Week 12. He brought in two of three targets for 43 yards, including a beautiful over-the-shoulder 31-yard touchdown, during Cincinnati's Week 11 defeat. Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase (5-31-0) were both held in check, but Higgins was able to reach the end zone for the sixth time in his last five games. He will aim to tally his first 100-yard outing since Week 8 against a New Orleans defense giving up 28.6 fantasy points per game (eighth) to WRs.

roster.name: Tony Pollard
roster.outlook: Tony Pollard rushed for 110 yards in the Titans' Week 11 loss to Dallas. His touchdown streak was halted at three games and six TDs, but he's up to 501 scrimmage yards over the past four games. Tennessee's entire offense has picked up the pace over that span, with QB Cam Ward stringing together his best three games of the season. Pollard faces a daunting Week 12 matchup against Jacksonville's elite run defense, but he navigated this matchup effectively in Week 10, setting season highs across the board with eight catches for 66 yards and a TD on nine targets to complement his modest 33 rushing yards on nine carries. You may as well keep rolling with the surging Pollard, though the tough opponent drops him to the low-end fantasy RB2 range for Week 12. With Tyjae Spears (knee) on IR, Pollard faces virtually zero competition for carries.

roster.name: Brandon Aubrey
roster.outlook: Brandon Aubrey made one field goal and six extra points last game for the Cowboys. Dallas destroyed Tennessee by a score of 51-30, though all the touchdowns left Aubrey with only a modest kicking performance. In fact, it was the first time in five outings that he failed to kick multiple field goals in a single game. In Week 12, Dallas will face division rival Philadelphia. The Eagles are allowing 23.7 points per tilt, which is 18th in the NFL.

roster.name: Aaron Jones Sr.
roster.outlook: Aaron Jones will look to keep his touchdown streak alive as the Vikings play the Falcons in Week 12. Jones rushed the ball eight times for 30 yards and a touchdown, and he caught one pass for 13 yards in a Week 11 loss to the 49ers. While the committee approach of Minnesota's backfield hasn't allowed for dominance for him or Jordan Mason, Jones has been the one to find the end zone more often. Atlanta has ranked 28th in fantasy points allowed to running backs this campaign.

roster.name: Khalil Shakir
roster.outlook: Khalil Shakir will be challenged to match Week 11's season-best outing when the Bills face the Chiefs in Week 12. With Dalton Kincaid sidelined in Week 11, Shakir turned nine targets into 101 yards, both season highs. With a quick turnaround to Week 12's Thursday affair hurting Kincaid's availability, Shakir could again see added looks, though against a much tougher secondary that's allowing the second-fewest fantasy points per game to wideouts.

roster.name: Isaiah Likely
roster.outlook: Isaiah Likely had an unexpectedly quiet game for the Giants last week.  Despite the win, Likely managed just one grab for 35 yards. he had a season-low three targets for the contest.  Likely is having a breakout campaign for the G-Men overall, though, so expect a return to normalcy in Week 12 versus the Colts. Indy is allowing 220.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 14th in the NFL. However, the Colts have also surrendered 20 throwing scores, which is 28th in the league.

roster.name: Xavier Worthy
roster.outlook: Xavier Worthy was finally able to make a splash in Kansas City's Week 11 win over the Cardinals, scoring his first touchdown since Week 2 on an 18-yard connection with Patrick Mahomes. Worthy caught just two of four targets for 38 total yards, and he's gone five straight games without reaching 50 receiving yards. The third-year speedster still has big-play upside, but he appears to be lost in the shuffle while Rashee Rice, Travis Kelce, running backs Kenneth Walker and Emmett Johnson, and newcomer Josh Downs all get prioritized ahead of him. Worthy will try to build on last week's effort in Week 12 against a Bills secondary that's tied for 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Bryce Young
roster.outlook: Bryce Young is expected to continue leading Carolina's offense into the Week 12 matchup against the Buccaneers. Young performed well during the Week 11 win over the Ravens, throwing for 254 yards, two touchdowns and an interception while posting his best single-game completion rate of the season (73.3%). Although Carolina has relied more on Chuba Hubbard and the rushing attack over the last couple of weeks, Young remains eighth in the NFL in pass attempts per game (36.8), which bodes well for his fantasy outlook rest-of-season. Despite this, Young could struggle against a solid Buccaneers defense that's allowed just 18.3 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.

roster.name: Cam Ward
roster.outlook: Cam Ward has thrown for at least 231 yards and two TDs in three consecutive games after failing to hit either of those passing benchmarks in any of his first seven starts this season. The 2025 first overall pick is growing in confidence, and he's also being forced to air it out as the 1-9 Titans consistently play catch-up. That's unlikely to change in Week 12, when the Titans face a Jaguars team that can put up points in bunches and is better at stopping the run than the pass. Ward's recent uptick in production has him in the conversation as a starter in superflex leagues, but there remain plenty of more reliable options in single-QB formats.
