roster.name: Derrick Henry
roster.outlook: In Week 12, Derrick Henry and the Ravens travel to Houston for an AFC showdown between playoff hopefuls. He rushed 13 times for 94 yards and a TD and caught four of five targets for 17 yards during Baltimore's Week 11 loss. Henry also lost a fumble, his second of the season, and was evaluated and cleared for a concussion in the fourth quarter. All signs point to him being good to go for the road tilt versus the Texans, who rank 14th in fantasy points allowed per game (21.4) to RBs.

roster.name: Brock Bowers
roster.outlook: Brock Bowers sat out the Raiders' Week 11 loss to the Broncos while dealing with quadriceps and ankle injuries. In his place, Michael Mayer caught just one of four targets, while Ian Thomas secured a one-yard touchdown from Fernando Mendoza. Bowers' absence prevented him from building more chemistry with the rookie quarterback, but the team is optimistic he'll be able to return in Week 12 and resume his spot as the clear No. 1 downfield option in the passing game. If Bowers does get cleared to return, he'll be facing a Browns defense that ranks 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

roster.name: Patrick Mahomes
roster.outlook: Patrick Mahomes continues to roll, tossing multiple touchdowns for a fourth straight game and topping 300 passing yards for the third time during that stretch in Kansas City's Week 11 win over the Cardinals. The two-time MVP finally seems to be back in top form after last season's knee injury, and the trade deadline addition of Josh Downs has given him another downfield option. Mahomes will need to stay hot in Week 12 in a marquee AFC clash against the Bills, who rank 10th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

roster.name: Harrison Butker
roster.outlook: Harrison Butker appears to be taking the threat to his job security seriously. The veteran kicker has been perfect over the last two weeks, converting both his field goal attempts and all nine of his PATs. He had missed seven FGs in 10 games, although six of those shanks have come from 50-plus yards out. With the Kansas City offense ramping up its efficiency, Butker's volume is likely to skew more toward extra points, giving him a safer floor at the expense of his ceiling. He'll look to stay locked in during a Week 12 clash with a Bills team that ranks ninth in points per game allowed.

roster.name: Michael Mayer
roster.outlook: Michael Mayer wasn't able to take advantage of Brock Bowers' absence during the Raiders' Week 11 loss to the Broncos, catching just one of four targets for a mere four yards. Depth tight end Ian Thomas also rubbed a little salt in the wound for Mayer's fantasy investors by catching a 19-yard touchdown from Fernando Mendoza. Bowers is expected back in Week 12, but even if he remains sidelined, Mayer's usage will make him a risky option, even against a Browns defense that ranks 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

roster.name: Keenan Allen
roster.outlook: Keenan Allen has served as a steadying presence in the 49ers' wideout corps ahead of a key NFC West clash against Seattle in Week 12. In his two games since joining San Francisco, Allen has caught eight passes for 99 yards on 11 targets, with seven of those catches resulting in a first down. The veteran wideout is one of many pass-catching mouths for QB Brock Purdy to feed, along with fellow vets Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and George Kittle. The team's WR corps will have to battle a tested Seahawks defense that has given up the second-fewest receptions per game (9.0) to wideouts this season.

roster.name: Devaughn Vele
roster.outlook: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain one of the Saints' top wideouts during the Week 12 matchup against the Bengals. Vele delivered a much-needed bounce-back performance during the Week 11 loss to the Bears, catching all seven of his targets for 76 yards. Despite playing behind Chris Olave, Vele appears to be a valuable portion of this New Orleans' offense and will likely compete for the No. 2 WR role with rookie Jordyn Tyson as the season progresses. Vele is still expected to struggle in Week 12 against a tough Bengals secondary that's given up just 10.2 yards per completion through nine games this season.

roster.name: Chase Brown
roster.outlook: Chase Brown and the Bengals welcome the Saints to town for an interconference showdown in Week 12. He had six carries for six yards and caught five of eight targets for 30 yards during Cincinnati's Week 11 defeat. Brown watched as Samaje Perine erupted for 97 scrimmage yards on 10 touches, as Brown was unable to build upon his two-TD performance from the previous outing. Next up is a juicy matchup against New Orleans' 31st-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (28.5) to opposing RBs.

roster.name: George Pickens
roster.outlook: George Pickens crossed the 100-yard threshold yet again for the Cowboys last game. Pickens caught seven passes for 102 yards and a touchdown in the 51-30 dismantling of the Titans. Pickens has gone over the 100-yard receiving mark in two-straight contests, having scored a gaudy four touchdowns during that span. In Week 12, the Cowboys will face a mediocre Eagles pass defense. Philadelphia is allowing 222.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 17th in the NFL. However, the Eagles have only given up 14 passing touchdowns, which is tied for ninth in the league.

roster.name: Germie Bernard
roster.outlook: Germie Bernard and the Steelers play host to the Broncos in a Week 12 clash on Black Friday. He caught six of 10 targets for 40 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 10 defeat. Bernard led his team in targets, tied for first in receptions, and finished third in yardage after failing to record a catch in his last outing. The talented rookie will look to build upon that performance versus a stout Denver defense that ranks sixth in fantasy points allowed per game (28.1) to opposing WRs.

roster.name: C.J. Stroud
roster.outlook: C.J. Stroud has thrown 16 touchdown passes in his last five games as he tries to carry the Texans and keep their playoff hopes alive. The surging QB is a top-10 fantasy option at his position in Week 12 against a reeling Ravens defense that has allowed at least 33 points in four of the past five games. Baltimore is on a six-game losing streak, which makes this game close to a must-win for the 4-6 Texans, who trail the Browns and Steelers by two games apiece and the Patriots by one game in the battle for the last two AFC wild-card spots. Houston has gotten subpar efficiency from its RBs, who are averaging a collective 3.6 yards per carry, so Stroud has routinely been asked to carry the offense. He has mostly been up to the task, ranking sixth in the league with 266 passing yards per game and tied for fourth with 22 touchdown passes.

roster.name: Stefon Diggs
roster.outlook: Stefon Diggs finished second on the team in targets last game for Washington. Diggs saw six looks en route to four catches for 45 yards in the thrilling 22-20 win over Cincy. Diggs has at least three catches in every game played this season, though has gone over 50 yards receiving on just three occasions. In Week 12, Diggs will face a lackluster Arizona pass defense. The Cardinals are allowing 226.4 passing yards per tilt, which is 20th in the NFL. In addition, the Cardinals have surrendered the most passing touchdowns in the league to date.

roster.name: Jonah Coleman
roster.outlook: Jonah Coleman cemented himself as the Broncos' No. 1 running back with a stunning performance in a Week 11 win over the Raiders. The fourth-round rookie romped for 129 scrimmage yards on 28 touches while scoring three rushing touchdowns, extending his streak of games with at least one score to three. Coleman appears capable of handling a bell-cow workload and a three-down role, but he could face competition for passing-down snaps once RJ Harvey is cleared to return from a knee injury. Coleman will face a Steelers defense in Week 12 that's tied for 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

roster.name: Devin Singletary
roster.outlook: Devin Singletary managed just two touches last game for the Giants. Singletary has just three touches over the last two contests, and even with starter Cam Skattebo fumbling, Singletary continues to serve mostly as depth. Singletary is also averaging just 2.9 yards per carry this season, which has not helped his cause. In Week 12, he could find some room to roam against the lowly Colts, though.  Indianapolis is allowing 134.4 rushing yards per tilt, which is 29th in the NFL.

roster.name: Christian McCaffrey
roster.outlook: Christian McCaffrey will look to extend his touchdown streak to 10 games when San Francisco faces Seattle in Week 12. Though McCaffrey finished with a modest 62 total yards in this past Sunday's win over Minnesota, he got into the end zone for the ninth straight game with a six-yard touchdown run. McCaffrey is tied for second in the NFL with 11 rushing TDs this season, and he's added three scores as a receiver. He figures to be challenged by a Seahawks defense that leads the NFL with just 3.16 yards per carry allowed to wideouts on the season.

roster.name: Omarion Hampton
roster.outlook: Omarion Hampton has re-established himself as the clear No. 1 option in the Chargers' backfield. Over the last three games, the second-year running back has turned 49 carries into 254 rushing yards and a touchdown, averaging a robust 5.2 yards per carry. Keaton Mitchell picked up a knee injury in a Week 11 loss to the Jets, which could leave Kimani Vidal as the primary backup. Hampton will look to keep surging in Week 12 against a Patriots defense that's tied for 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

roster.name: Chris Olave
roster.outlook: Chris Olave is expected to remain the Saints' top wideout during the Week 12 matchup against the Bengals. Olave bounced back from a poor Week 10 performance in last week's loss to the Bears, catching nine of 15 targets to 102 yards. He remains one of seven NFL players to average 10-or-more targets per game (10.2) while ranking seventh in the league in receiving yards per game (86.6). Despite his impressive season, Olave could struggle in Week 12 against a solid Bengals secondary that's given up just 29.7 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts through nine games this season.

roster.name: Jaylen Waddle
roster.outlook: Jaylen Waddle continues to struggle to make a big difference in the Broncos' passing game. In a Week 11 win over the Raiders, the former Dolphin caught three of six targets for 61 yards, his highest yardage total since Week 2. Waddle is on pace to record fewer than 700 receiving yards in a season for the first time, and with the Denver offense leaning more heavily on rookie running back Jonah Coleman, Bo Nix hasn't had to air it out much. Waddle seems unlikely to break out in Week 12 against a Steelers secondary that ranks 12th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Jayden Daniels
roster.outlook: Jayden Daniels did not record a touchdown last game for the Commanders.  However, he threw for 289 yards and rushed for an additional 55 yards in the surprising 22-20 win over the Bengals. It was the second-highest passing total of the season for Daniels, and his third-highest rushing total of the year. Daniels has a tasty matchup in Week 12 versus a suspect Cardinals defense allowing 355.2 scrimmage yards per game, which is 26th in the NFL. In addition, Arizona is allowing 29.4 points per tilt, which is 31st in the league.

roster.name: George Kittle
roster.outlook: George Kittle enters San Francisco's Week 12 clash against Seattle fresh off a two-touchdown performance in Mexico City. While Kittle caught just three passes (on three targets) this past Sunday versus the Vikings, two of those receptions resulted in touchdowns. Kittle is up to seven scores on the season, tied for the most among NFL tight ends. With that said, Seattle has allowed just two TDs to tight ends this season and is giving up the third-fewest fantasy points per game (5.5) to the position, so Kittle faces a stiff task in replicating his Week 11 performance.

roster.name: Rhamondre Stevenson
roster.outlook: Rhamondre Stevenson could see heavy volume for the Patriots in Week 12 against the Chargers, with Tommy DeVito unlikely to spark the passing game. Emerging from a Week 11 bye, Stevenson can hopefully avoid an injury designation after a knee issue limited him to 36 yards on 12 carries over his last two outings. Facing a stacked front, Stevenson will rely on volume to beat a defense that's allowing 4.1 yards per carry and 10 touchdowns to backs in as many games, landing him in RB2/flex territory.

roster.name: Josh Downs
roster.outlook: Josh Downs has seen very consistent usage in his two games with Kansas City, catching four passes on five targets in each with yardage in the 50s. The main difference was a touchdown in Week 10, something he wasn't able to repeat in a Week 11 win over the Cardinals. Downs is adapting quickly to his new offense, but Patrick Mahomes has plenty of other options in Rashee Rice, Travis Kelce, Xavier Worthy, and running backs Kenneth Walker and Emmett Johnson. Downs will look to continue building chemistry with Mahomes in Week 12 against a Bills secondary that's tied for 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

roster.name: Jake Bates
roster.outlook: Jake Bates will look to tighten up as the Lions play the Bears in Week 12. Bates was mostly solid in a Week 11 win over the Buccaneers, but he did miss a 53-yard field goal in the first quarter. Either way, the third-year boot has now converted 17 of 19 field-goal attempts and nailed all 33 of his XPAs across 10 games this season. He'll face a Chicago defense that's a tough second in fantasy points allowed to kickers this season.

roster.name: Dominic Zvada
roster.outlook: Dominic Zvada missed yet another field goal last game for the Giants. The inconsistent rookie actually connected on three field goals from 40-plus yards out, but somehow missed a 32-yarder in the 23-18 win over the Jags. It was the seventh miss of the season for Zvada, which is tied for the league-lead. Zvada still appears to have his job heading into Week 12 versus the Colts, though. Indy is allowing 27 points per game, which is 28th in the NFL.

roster.name: Samaje Perine
roster.outlook: Samaje Perine and the Bengals return home to host the 3-7 Saints in Week 12. He had six carries for 26 yards and caught all four targets for 71 yards during Cincinnati's Week 11 defeat. Perine finished with one fewer touch than starter Chase Brown, but Perine was much more productive. Perine could be a sneaky fantasy play versus a New Orleans defense allowing 28.5 fantasy points per game (31st) to opposing RBs.

roster.name: Antonio Williams
roster.outlook: Antonio Williams had a breakout performance last game for the Commanders. Williams snagged nine passes for 122 yards in the thrilling 22-20 win over the Bengals. This included several big catches down the stretch, including a 42-yarder from quarterback Jayden Daniels to put the Commanders in field goal range for the game-winning kick. Williams received a career-high 11 targets. In Week 12, Williams will face a lackluster Arizona pass defense. The Cardinals are allowing 226.4 passing yards per tilt, which is 20th in the NFL. In addition, the Cardinals have surrendered the most passing touchdowns in the league to date.

free_agents.name: Davante Adams
free_agents.outlook: Davante Adams (hamstring) is expected to remain sidelined for the Rams' Week 12 clash against Green Bay. That may be due in part to the game taking part on Wednesday, but even with an extended break afterward, the star wideout is currently thought to have just an "outside chance" to suit up in Week 13 against Kansas City. Los Angeles will turn to a hodgepodge of wideouts, including Konata Mumpfield, CJ Daniels, Tutu Atwell and Xavier Smith, for wideout production in the absence of Adams and Puka Nacua (knee/toe).

free_agents.name: Will Reichard
free_agents.outlook: Will Reichard will look to bounce back as the Vikings play the Falcons in Week 12. Reichard went 1-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made one XPA in a Week 11 loss to the 49ers. Fortunately, those misses were just his second and third of the season, so there aren't currently any blaring warning signs of regression. He'll face a Falcons squad that's ranked top 10 versus fantasy kickers this campaign.

free_agents.name: Matthew Stafford
free_agents.outlook: Matthew Stafford emerges from the Rams' bye with the prospect of facing Green Bay in Week 12 still without either of his two top wideouts. Davante Adams (hamstring) isn't expected to come off IR this week, and Puka Nacua (knee/toe) is slated to miss the remainder of the campaign. Stafford was able to guide Los Angeles to a win without both stars in Week 10 against Arizona, throwing for 249 yards with three touchdowns and one interception, but he'll likely face a tougher challenge this week. Whereas the Cardinals rank 30th in the NFL in fantasy points per game allowed to quarterbacks, the Packers sit at a very respectable eighth in that category.

free_agents.name: Jalen Coker
free_agents.outlook: Jalen Coker (concussion) is expected to remain one of Carolina's top weapons if active for the Week 12 matchup against the Buccaneers. Coker entered concussion protocol following a four-catch, 47 yard performance in a win over the Ravens in Week 11, putting his availability for Monday night's contest in jeopardy. He's been relatively underwhelming over his last five games, catching 11 of 25 targets for 121 yards and one touchdown. If active, Coker will likely struggle against an impressive Tampa Bay secondary that's given up just 7.6 yards per target to opposing wideouts this season.

free_agents.name: Dallas Goedert
free_agents.outlook: Dallas Goedert had a rather quiet output for the Eagles with the return of DeVonta Smith. While Smith managed a healthy 12 targets in the 19-16 win over the Steelers, Goedert had just one look for the entire game. However, said target did gain 38 yards through the air.  Brighter days could be ahead for Goedert, though, as the Eagles face a porous Dallas Cowboys defense in Week 12. Dallas is allowing 237.9 passing yards per tilt, which is 28th in the league. "America's Team" has also given up 21 passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 29th in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Rico Dowdle
free_agents.outlook: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers welcome the Broncos to town for a Week 12 meeting on Black Friday. He rushed five times for 15 yards and hauled in four of five targets for 19 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 11 loss. Dowdle again trailed Jaylen Warren in backfield touches, as the former earned nine to the latter's 11. Dowdle will look to make the most of his opportunities against Denver's 25th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (24.9) to RBs.

free_agents.name: Chris Boswell
free_agents.outlook: Chris Boswell and the Steelers aim to improve to 5-0 at home when they host the Broncos in Week 12 on Black Friday. He went 3-for-3 on field goal attempts and drilled his lone PAT during Pittsburgh's 19-16 loss in Week 11. Boswell has now converted all of his field goals in consecutive games for the first time all season. The veteran kicker will try to stay perfect versus a Denver defense allowing 21.0 points per game through 10 outings.

free_agents.name: Rachaad White
free_agents.outlook: Rachaad White dressed last game for the Commanders, but did not record a carry. Perhaps his heel issue was more concerning than initially thought, as Jacory Croskey-Merritt had 13 carries against the Bengals, while Austin Ekeler registered seven. Croskey-Merritt's return from injury likely relegates White to backup duty in Week 12 versus Arizona anyway, though the matchup is extremely favorable. The Cardinals are allowing 128.8 rushing yards per clash, which is 27th in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Tyler Shough
free_agents.outlook: Tyler Shough is expected to continue leading the Saints' offense into the Week 12 matchup against the Bengals. Shough has been held in check over the last two weeks, averaging 204.5 passing yards, one touchdown and one interception per game during that stretch. Despite this, Shough ranks second in the NFL in pass attempts per game (38.5), suggesting more fantasy value is imminent as the season progresses. Additionally, he's in for a favorable Week 12 matchup against a Bengals defense that's allowed 20.9 fantasy points per game through nine contests this season.

free_agents.name: Kenny Gainwell
free_agents.outlook: Kenny Gainwell is expected to operate as Tampa Bay's No. 2 running back during the Week 12 matchup against the Panthers. Despite playing behind Bucky Irving, Gainwell has emerged as one of the top playmakers on this Buccaneers offense. Over the team's last four contests, Gainwell has averaged 90.8 scrimmage yards per game but hasn't found the end zone. He could be a valuable fantasy asset in Week 12, as Tampa Bay is set to face a Carolina defense that's allowed the most fantasy points per game to opposing running backs (28.6) in the NFL this year.

free_agents.name: J.K. Dobbins
free_agents.outlook: J.K. Dobbins has faded into a depth role in the Broncos' backfield with the emergence of rookie Jonah Coleman. Dobbins has handled single-digit touches in four straight games, and in a Week 11 win over the Raiders, he saw only one snap on offense, gaining zero yards on his only carry. The veteran's main path to fantasy relevance was through volume, and that no longer appears to be open while Coleman is healthy and effective. Dobbins will try to win back a little more work in Week 12 against a Steelers defense that's tied for 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

free_agents.name: Tank Dell
free_agents.outlook: Tank Dell has just six catches for 48 yards in two games since his 105-yard outburst in Week 9, which included a 63-yard touchdown catch. A Week 12 home game against the Ravens offers Dell a chance to showcase his ability to generate big plays, as Baltimore's struggling defense has allowed at least 33 points to four of its last five opponents. Dell has a high enough ceiling to warrant flex consideration in most formats, though his floor remains shaky as he competes for targets in a deep Texans WR room that also includes Nico Collins, Xavier Hutchinson, Kayshon Boutte (hip), and Marvin Harrison (hamstring).

free_agents.name: Jacory Croskey-Merritt
free_agents.outlook: Jacory Croskey-Merritt found the end zone in his return from injury for the Commanders.  Bill rushed 13 times for 54 yards and the score in the surprising 22-20 win over the Bengals. He nearly doubled up backup Austin Ekeler in terms of carries. Croskey-Merritt also caught two passes for 23 yards out of the backfield. Bill looks to be the featured back heading into a juicy matchup with the Cardinals. Arizona is allowing 128.8 rushing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the league. Likewise, Arizona has yielded 12 rushing touchdowns on the season, which is tied for 22nd in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Jason Myers
free_agents.outlook: Jason Myers is in the midst of a quiet campaign heading into Seattle's matchup versus the 49ers in Week 12. After making a career-high 41 field goals over 17 regular-season games last year, the veteran kicker is well off the pace for reaching that mark in 2026, as he's made a modest 16 FGs (on 19 attempts) through 10 contests. Myers has at least continued to be accurate, and he's converted all three of his attempts from 50-plus yards. San Francisco has allowed 24 field-goal attempts this season, tied for eighth-most in the league, so Myers could be a bit busier Sunday.

free_agents.name: Tyler Allgeier
free_agents.outlook: Tyler Allgeier may be losing his grasp on the Cardinals' starting RB role ahead of a Week 12 matchup versus the Commanders. Allgeier couldn't get much going this past Sunday in a loss to Kansas City, managing just 23 yards on seven carries. Meanwhile, Bam Knight gained 45 yards on eight touches, and it's possible that Jeremiyah Love (ankle) will return to action soon. Washington has been pretty solid against the run this season, yielding just 3.67 yards per carry to running backs, the eighth-best mark in the league.

free_agents.name: DeMario Douglas
free_agents.outlook: DeMario Douglas has an uncertain role ahead of the Patriots' Week 12 matchup against the Chargers. Douglas was held to a season-low three-yard catch in Week 10 with Drake Maye injured on the opening drive. The Week 11 bye is likely not sufficient for Douglas and new QB Tommy DeVito to develop a rapport. The Chargers offer an exploitable matchup, allowing 9.1 yards per target, but Douglas' volume will be in question, suggesting a wait-and-see approach is prudent.

free_agents.name: Marvin Harrison Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Marvin Harrison hasn't suited up since Week 9 due to a hamstring injury. Even if he returns in Week 12 against the Ravens, Harrison will be tough to trust considering he has just six catches for 60 yards and one touchdown in three appearances for Houston. Fellow Houston wideouts Nico Collins, Xavier Hutchinson, Tank Dell and Kayshon Boutte (hip) are all more likely to capitalize on facing the reeling Ravens defense, which has allowed at least 33 points in four of the last five games.

free_agents.name: Hunter Henry
free_agents.outlook: Hunter Henry is saddled with an unfavorable Week 12 matchup when the Patriots take on the Chargers. He has just three targets in each of New England's last three games. Tommy DeVito playing quarterback could lead to additional check-downs, but that wasn't the case in Week 10 against Detroit. The Chargers have allowed one touchdown to a tight end, though a league-high 9.4 yards per target. Still, Henry isn't set up for a productive effort.

free_agents.name: Adonai Mitchell
free_agents.outlook: Adonai Mitchell remains an inconsistent, high-upside option in the Jets' low-volume passing game ahead of a Week 12 matchup with the Dolphins. Mitchell has three or fewer catches in four of five games since returning from a four-game injury absence, and the Jets have now failed to complete 20 passes for three straight games. Miami's secondary is vertically vulnerable, allowing 9.2 yards per target. The Dolphins are vulnerable to the run, and the Jets prefer to grind it out, so Mitchell will be a boom-or-bust option, likely excluding him from fantasy lineups.

free_agents.name: Pat Freiermuth
free_agents.outlook: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers battle the Broncos at home on Black Friday in Week 12. He caught all five targets for 39 yards and rushed once for one yard during Pittsburgh's Week 11 loss. Freiermuth has recently been more involved on offense than fellow tight end Darnell Washington as Washington finished with a 3-22-0 line on three targets. Freiermuth remains a TD-or-bust fantasy option and he'll face a Denver defense that's allowed the third-most receiving yards (702) and eight TDs (T-27th) to opposing TEs in 2026.

free_agents.name: Makai Lemon
free_agents.outlook: Makai Lemon had a quiet output for the Eagles with the return of DeVonta Smith. While Smith managed a healthy 12 targets in the 19-16 win over the Steelers, Lemon had just three looks for the game. Lemon finished with just one reception for three yards.  Brighter days could be ahead for Lemon, though, as the Eagles face a porous Dallas Cowboys defense in Week 12. Dallas is allowing 237.9 passing yards per tilt, which is 28th in the league. "America's Team" has also given up 21 passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 29th in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Xavier Hutchinson
free_agents.outlook: Xavier Hutchinson has topped 30 yards just once in Houston's last five games. He had a three-game touchdown streak to buoy his stat line during that stretch, but the scoring binge was likely fool's gold for a fourth-year player who had just three career TDs prior to that streak, which was snapped in the Week 11 win over Indianapolis. Starting a new scoring streak won't be easy in Week 12 against a Ravens defense that has held WRs to just seven touchdowns. While the Ravens are giving up 162 yards per game to the position, Hutchinson is competing for targets with Nico Collins and Tank Dell, as well as possibly Kayshon Boutte (hip) and Marvin Harrison (hamstring). Considering that Hutchinson's 6.3 yards per target are second-fewest among that group, ahead of only Harrison, it's tough to trust Hutchinson as anything more than a deep-league flex-spot flier.

free_agents.name: Ryan Flournoy
free_agents.outlook: Ryan Flournoy was not invited to the party last game for the Cowboys. While CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens each had over 100 yards receiving and a touchdown in the win over the Titans, Flournoy caught just one pass for 11 yards. It was his lowest output of the season. In Week 12, Flournoy will look to get back on track versus a mediocre Eagles pass defense. Philadelphia is allowing 222.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 17th in the NFL. However, the Eagles have only given up 14 passing touchdowns, which is tied for ninth in the league.

free_agents.name: Omar Cooper Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Omar Cooper's role in the Jets' offense remains inconsistent ahead of a Week 12 matchup with the Dolphins, and his availability remains in question due to ankle and hip woes. Over his last five healthy games, Cooper has no catches in two of them and a combined 19 in the other three outings. He compiled 115 receiving yards and a touchdown against Miami earlier in the year, and their secondary is allowing 9.2 yards per target to receivers, the fifth-highest mark in the league. Cooper is a high-ceiling speculative play if he suits up.

free_agents.name: Kaelon Black
free_agents.outlook: Kaelon Black will face another tough run defense when the 49ers host the Seahawks in Week 12. Black couldn't do much against the Vikings' vaunted defense this past Sunday, gaining just eight yards on six carries while adding seven yards on his lone reception. He also saw a three-game streak of double-digit touches snapped, but the rookie maintained a steady 30% offensive snap share. Black and the 49ers' running game as a whole should be challenged by a Seahawks defense that ranks seventh in the NFL with 15.1 fantasy points per game allowed to running backs.

free_agents.name: Michael Pittman Jr.
free_agents.outlook: In Week 12, Michael Pittman and Pittsburgh aim to snap a two-game losing skid when they host the Broncos on Black Friday. He hasn't played since Week 4 after being placed on injured reserve due to a foot injury, but the first-year Steeler is ready to make his return versus a talented Denver secondary, which is allowing 28.1 fantasy points per game to WRs. Pittman hasn't played in nearly two months, so fantasy managers needing help at receiver should look elsewhere until he can prove otherwise.

free_agents.name: Caleb Douglas
free_agents.outlook: Caleb Douglas is emerging as the top option in Miami's limited passing game ahead of a Week 12 matchup with the Jets. He amassed a career-high 10 targets in Week 11 but brought in only two of them, finishing with 30 yards. The Dolphins have failed to reach the end zone through the air in two games with Kyle McCord at the helm, but Douglas brings volume into Week 12. He solved the Jets with two touchdowns and 70 yards on just two receptions in Week 7, but given McCord's volatility, lowering Douglas on your wide receiver depth chart is prudent in Week 12. Douglas is a high-upside WR/flex.

free_agents.name: Juwan Johnson
free_agents.outlook: Juwan Johnson (hamstring) is expected to remain the Saints' top tight end if active for the Week 12 matchup against the Bengals. Johnson sustained a hamstring injury during the Week 11 loss to the Bears, and the extent of the issue remains TBD. Johnson struggled to find fantasy value before sustaining this injury, catching just five of 10 targets for 69 yards and one touchdown from Weeks 7 through 10 (three games). If active, Johnson could find fantasy value but is likely still too inconsistent to start, even with a favorable matchup against a Bengals defense that's given up 15.2 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.

free_agents.name: Matt Gay
free_agents.outlook: Matt Gay has been perfect over the last four weeks, going 5-for-5 on field goal attempts and 11-for-11 on PATs. The veteran kicker's volume hasn't been significantly affected by the switch at quarterback from Kirk Cousins to Fernando Mendoza, and the Raiders' offense might actually take a step forward once Brock Bowers gets healthy, with young skill players Ashton Jeanty and Jack Bech showing signs of breaking out. Gay will look to stay locked in during Week 12's clash with a Browns team that's allowing 22.0 points per game, tied for 14th in the league.

free_agents.name: Mike Gesicki
free_agents.outlook: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals look to extend their three-game win streak at home versus the Saints in Week 12. He caught five of six targets for a team-high 77 yards during Cincinnati's Week 11 loss. Gesicki finished third on the team in targets and matched Ja'Marr Chase and Chase Brown for the team lead in receptions. The outing was impressive considering Joe Burrow attempted 40 passes and threw for 300 yards, with Ja'Marr Chase (5-31-0) and Tee Higgins (2-43-1) combining for only 74 of them. Gesicki will attempt to punish a New Orleans defense allowing the seventh-most fantasy points per game (15.7) to TEs.

free_agents.name: Brian Thomas Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Brian Thomas has just 84 receiving yards in his last eight games. He has scored three times over that span, giving Thomas an inkling of deep-league fantasy appeal in Jacksonville's Week 12 home matchup against a Titans defense that has allowed the most production in the league to wide receivers. Thomas tied his season high with three catches in the Jaguars' Week 10 win at Tennessee, though he posted just 29 receiving yards. Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers are far more likely to capitalize on this favorable matchup.

free_agents.name: Malik Washington
free_agents.outlook: Malik Washington brings steady but middling production for the Dolphins into a Week 12 matchup with the Jets. For the fourth time in five games since Miami's Week 6 bye, Washington caught three passes in Week 11, finishing with just 30 yards. With Caleb Douglas emerging as Miami's top option, their low-success passing game hasn't proven capable of sustaining multiple receivers. The Jets are allowing 7.6 yard per target, ranking towards the bottom portion of the middle-tier, not suggesting Washington can break out on limited opportunities.

free_agents.name: Dalton Schultz
free_agents.outlook: Dalton Schultz has been held to one catch for 11 yards in each of Houston's last two games, though one of those receptions was his first touchdown of the season. He has been utilized primarily as a blocker in Houston's recent games, so Schultz hasn't benefited much from the strong play of QB C.J. Stroud. In Week 12, Schultz will face a Ravens defense that has struggled to defend TEs, allowing 54 yards per game and seven TDs in 11 games to the position. He's a viable low-end starter at a position that lacks depth, but nobody's getting excited about starting Schultz these days.

free_agents.name: Justice Hill
free_agents.outlook: Justice Hill and the Ravens are on the road for a Week 12 meeting with the Texans. He had six carries for 69 yards and a touchdown and caught four of five targets for 27 yards during Baltimore's Week 11 loss. Hill lost a fumble but was otherwise very productive with his 10 total touches, as he's now recorded two TDs in his last three games. He'll aim to keep contributing against a Houston defense allowing 21.4 fantasy points per game (14th) to RBs.

free_agents.name: Jake Ferguson
free_agents.outlook: Jake Ferguson is unlikely to suit up in Week 12 for the Cowboys due to lingering knee and ankle issues. Ferguson was having a down year prior to the injury, recording just 19 catches for 136 yards and four touchdowns.  In Week 12, Brevyn Spann-Ford will operate once again as the No. 1 tight end versus a mediocre Eagles pass defense. Philadelphia is allowing 222.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 17th in the NFL. However, the Eagles have only given up 14 passing touchdowns, which is tied for ninth in the league.

free_agents.name: Cairo Santos
free_agents.outlook: Cairo Santos will enter a tough matchup as the Bears play the Lions in Week 12. Santos missed a PAT in a Week 11 win over the Saints, but he converted both of his field-goal attempts. The veteran kicker has now made two or more field goals in each of his last four games. He'll take on a Detroit squad that's ranked first in fantasy points allowed to his position.

free_agents.name: Jason Sanders
free_agents.outlook: JJason Sanders continues to get multiple scoring opportunities for the Jets ahead of a Week 12 matchup with the Dolphins. For the fourth consecutive week and fifth time in six games, Sanders made at least two field goals, giving him 19 in that stretch to go with nine extra points. The outlier was a Week 7 matchup with Miami, as the Jets played from behind and chose not to kick. With Kyle McCord under center for Miami in Week 12, that's not a likely script, suggesting Sanders can again be busy against a defense allowing the fifth-most fantasy points per game to kickers.

free_agents.name: Fernando Mendoza
free_agents.outlook: Fernando Mendoza is beginning to show why he was the first overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. In the Raiders' Week 11 loss to the Broncos, the rookie quarterback threw his first three career touchdown passes, and he did it without Brock Bowers in the lineup. Instead, Jack Bech emerged as his top target, while Mendoza's other two scores went to depth tight end Ian Thomas and running back Ashton Jeanty. Mendoza will look to secure his first win as a starter in Week 12 against a Browns defense that ranks seventh in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

free_agents.name: Kyler Murray
free_agents.outlook: Kyler Murray will look to get healthy in Week 12 as the Vikings play the Falcons. Murray hasn't seen the field since a Week 8 loss to Detroit, and the Vikings' trade for Kirk Cousins has essentially erased his value at this point in the season. If healthy, he'll aim to take away Minnesota's current backup role from veteran Carson Wentz.

free_agents.name: J.J. McCarthy
free_agents.outlook: J.J. McCarthy tossed a touchdown pass for the second-straight game for the Giants.  However, it was only the third touchdown pass in five outings for McCarthy. He has rushed for at least 22 yards in four of those five contests, though has yet to find the end zone with his legs. In Week 12, the Giants will face a Colts defense that has struggled mightily in 2026. Indianapolis currently ranks in the bottom five in the NFL in terms of rushing yards allowed, passing touchdowns surrendered and overall points yielded this season.

free_agents.name: MarShawn Lloyd
free_agents.outlook: MarShawn Lloyd's role is up in the air as the Packers play the Rams in Week 12. Lloyd hasn't done much in a crowded backfield so far this season, with it looking like receiving work may be his only path to fantasy relevance at this point in the year. The Rams have also ranked a tough third in fantasy points allowed to RBs, which could make it hard for Lloyd to put together anything noteworthy.

free_agents.name: Deshaun Watson
free_agents.outlook: Deshaun Watson and the Browns host the Raiders in a Week 12 showdown on Sunday Night Football. During Cleveland's Week 10 victory, he threw for 312 yards (25-of-40) with zero TDs and one INT, and had eight carries for 49 yards and a TD. Watson spread the ball around to nine different receivers to help lead a comeback win, but he's now failed to record a TD pass in four straight outings. That streak could come to an end as Las Vegas allows 23.8 fantasy points per game (29th) to QBs and has given up the second-most passing TDs (23) this season.

free_agents.name: Evan McPherson
free_agents.outlook: In Week 12, Evan McPherson and the Bengals will attempt to extend a three-game home win streak when the Saints come to town. He went 2-for-2 on both field goal and extra point attempts during Cincinnati's Week 11 loss. McPherson's 56-yard field goal with less than a minute remaining gave the Bengals the lead, but only for the time being, as their five-game win streak was snapped in the end. He bounced back nicely after missing his first kick of the season in Week 10, and McPherson will continue earning plenty of scoring opportunities in Cincinnati's high-powered offense.

free_agents.name: Dylan Sampson
free_agents.outlook: Dylan Sampson and the Browns host the Raiders on Sunday Night Football in Week 12. He rushed four times for six yards and caught four of six targets for 31 yards during Cleveland's Week 10 victory. Sampson was out-touched 13-8 by starter Quinshon Judkins, but Sampson continues to push closer to an even timeshare. Sampson will look to contribute more versus a Las Vegas defense allowing 26.9 fantasy points per game to RBs, the fifth most in the league.

free_agents.name: Travis Hunter
free_agents.outlook: Travis Hunter is unlikely to get enough touches in Week 12 to capitalize on facing a league-worst Titans secondary that's giving up 16 catches for 210 yards per game to WRs. He has caught multiple passes just twice all season for the Jaguars while growing into one of the league's best cornerbacks on the other side of the ball. With Jacksonville's WR room healthy entering Week 12, expect Hunter to be limited to a handful of snaps on offense as usual.

free_agents.name: Chris Rodriguez Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Chris Rodriguez could make a spot start for the Jaguars in a juicy Week 12 matchup against the 1-9 Titans if Bhayshul Tuten (ankle) sits out, in which case Rodriguez would have fantasy RB2 upside. If Tuten suits up, Rodriguez would remain in the deep-league flex conversation as Jacksonville's change-of-pace RB against a Tennessee defense that has allowed 44.7 points per game in its last three. The Jaguars scored 40 points against the Titans in Week 10, though Rodriguez was limited to a season-low five rushing yards in that game while Tuten racked up 113 scrimmage yards and a TD.

free_agents.name: Quentin Johnston
free_agents.outlook: Quentin Johnston was nearly invisible again in the Chargers' Week 11 loss to the Jets. The fourth-year wideout has caught one pass in three straight games and five of his last six, as Mike McDaniel's quick-strike offensive scheme doesn't give him enough time to get downfield on the deep routes that have been his bread and butter. Johnston could be catching passes from DJ Uiagalelei instead of Justin Herbert due to the starting QB's concussion, but it's not like his outlook could get much worse. Johnston will try to take advantage of whatever target volume he gets in Week 12 against a Patriots secondary that ranks an enticing 31st in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

free_agents.name: Baker Mayfield
free_agents.outlook: Baker Mayfield is expected to continue leading Tampa Bay's offense during the Week 12 matchup against the Panthers. Mayfield battled through foot and thumb injuries during the Week 11 loss to the Lions, throwing for 187 yards and two touchdowns. The veteran quarterback has struggled this season, averaging just 158.4 passing yards per game while accounting for six total touchdowns and seven turnovers in seven games. He will likely struggle against the Panthers' defense in Week 12, as Carolina has allowed just 19.8 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.

free_agents.name: Sam Darnold
free_agents.outlook: Sam Darnold (quad/ribs) is expected to return as Seattle's starting QB for the team's Week 12 matchup against San Francisco. Darnold missed the Seahawks' past two games due to the pair of injuries, but he's line to return following the club's Week 11 bye. If that does indeed happen, Drew Lock is likely to return to the backup role despite playing well during Darnold's absence. Whoever ultimately starts will face a 49ers defense that has given up an 89.1 QB rating this season to rank 15th in the NFL in that category.

free_agents.name: Chad Ryland
free_agents.outlook: Chad Ryland has lacked opportunities of late as the Cardinals' Week 12 matchup versus Washington approaches. Ryland hasn't had more than two field-goal tries in four straight games, and he's been limited to just one extra-point attempt in his past three contests. That's because Arizona's offense is sputtering, having scored just 16 points over its past three games. Ryland will look for more opportunities against the Commanders, who have shown some improvements on defense this year but still rank 20th in the NFL with 24.8 points allowed per contest.

free_agents.name: Corey Kiner
free_agents.outlook: Corey Kiner brings double-digit touch potential into the Patriots' Week 12 game against the Chargers, as New England will likely run often with Tommy DeVito playing quarterback. The Chargers are allowing a modest 4.1 yards per carry but 10 touchdowns to running backs in 10 games, and six have topped 50 yards over the last five games. Kiner's lack of involvement in the passing game, paired with facing many eight-man fronts, tempers optimism, but opportunity should be available.

free_agents.name: Mike Washington Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Mike Washington has faded into a depth role in the Raiders' backfield. With Ashton Jeanty looking more effective on the ground, Washington has handled single-digit carries in three straight games, managing 62 rushing yards on 23 total totes. The rookie running back would likely need a Jeanty injury to get another shot at the top spot on early downs. Washington will face a Browns defense in Week 12 that ranks 12th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

free_agents.name: Rashid Shaheed
free_agents.outlook: Rashid Shaheed enters Seattle's Week 12 matchup against San Francisco looking for his first big game of the campaign. Shaheed returned from a two-game absence to suit up against the Raiders in Week 10 but managed just one catch for eight yards on two targets. The speedy wideout doesn't yet have a receiving touchdown this season, and he's topped out at five catches and 66 yards, though he's added value with occasional carries and especially with his work as a punt and kickoff returner. Shaheed may be dependent on big plays to put up useful fantasy production, and the 49ers have given up just 27 receptions of 20-plus yards this season, tied for ninth-fewest in the league.

free_agents.name: Geno Smith
free_agents.outlook: Geno Smith brings low-volume but surging efficiency into the Jets' Week 12 matchup with the Dolphins. While he hasn't topped 176 passing yards in three straight games and has failed to complete more than 18 attempts, Smith is coming off his third three-touchdown pass outing in Week 11. With the Jets preferring a run-first approach paired with an unhealthy receiving corps, Smith is not a fantasy option against a mid-tier secondary that's allowing 7.7 yards per attempt.

free_agents.name: Jayden Reed
free_agents.outlook: Jayden Reed will remain out as the Packers play the Rams in Week 12. Reed sustained a neck injury against the Jets in Week 2, which requires season-ending surgery. His absence should continue to pave the way for Savion Williams, Bo Melton and J. Michael Sturdivant to get more opportunities in Green Bay's passing game.

free_agents.name: Mack Hollins
free_agents.outlook: Mack Hollins is slated for an uptick in opportunity but with sketchy quarterback play when the Patriots face the Chargers in Week 12. He hauled in five catches for 48 yards in Week 10 despite losing Drake Maye on the opening drive and Tommy DeVito completing just 12 passes for 81 yards in relief. It's unlikely that DeVito airs it out, but with A.J. Brown (hamstring) likely out and the Chargers allowing 13 touchdowns and 9.1 yards per target to opposing wideouts, Hollins could surprise.

free_agents.name: Keon Coleman
free_agents.outlook: Keon Coleman doesn't draw enough of Josh Allen's attention to be a reliable fantasy option when the Bills face the Chiefs in Week 12. Despite Allen throwing a season-high 45 times in Week 11, Coleman brought in only two of four targets, finishing with 17 yards, tying a four-game high. Kansas City is allowing a mere 6.6 yards per target and has given up only three touchdown catches to wideouts. This is not the week for Coleman to emerge.

free_agents.name: Elic Ayomanor
free_agents.outlook: Elic Ayomanor was surprisingly quiet in Tennessee's 51-30 loss to Dallas in Week 11. Chimere Dike, Calvin Ridley and Carnell Tate each had at least five targets and 58 yards, while Ayomanor settled for 27 yards on three catches in the first game after Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) was placed on IR. Titans QB Cam Ward has been spreading the ball around, and Ayomanor had his moment in Week 10 with 79 yards on 10 targets against the Jaguars, but the second-year wideout hasn't exceeded three catches in any other game this season. Expectations should be tempered in the Week 12 road rematch against a Jacksonville defense that ranks among the league's best units overall but in the middle of the pack against the pass. Ayomanor isn't an appealing flex option outside of deeper formats.

free_agents.name: Wil Lutz
free_agents.outlook: Wil Lutz failed to kick multiple field goals for the first time in over a month during the Broncos' Week 11 win over the Raiders, but he made up for it with a season-high five PATs. The veteran kicker has been perfect over the last five contests, going 9-for-9 on FG attempts and 14-for-14 on extra points, giving him a solid floor but shaky ceiling while supporting an underperforming Denver offense. Lutz will look to keep rolling in Week 12 against a Steelers team that ranks seventh in points per game allowed, but which has allowed a league-high 30 FG attempts through 10 games.

free_agents.name: Konata Mumpfield
free_agents.outlook: Konata Mumpfield appears set for at least one more game as the Rams' de facto No. 1 wideout in Week 12 against Green Bay. Puka Nacua (knee/toe) is expected to miss the rest of the season, and Davante Adams (hamstring) is slated to remain on IR this week, leaving Los Angeles' WR corps in the hands of Mumpfield, CJ Daniels, Tutu Atwell and Xavier Smith. Mumpfield was the most productive of the group in Week 10 against Arizona, posting three catches for 81 yards on four targets. He'll look to build more momentum against the Packers, who rank 23rd in the league with 22.1 fantasy points per game allowed to wideouts.

free_agents.name: Seth McGowan
free_agents.outlook: Seth McGowan injured his hamstring in the Colts' Week 11 loss to Houston and is expected to sit out Week 12 against the Giants. The rookie had been earning a larger share of carries in a change-of-pace role behind Jonathan Taylor. DJ Giddens moves up to the second spot on Indianapolis' RB depth chart, but he may not get as many opportunities as McGowan did.

free_agents.name: Jacoby Brissett
free_agents.outlook: Jacoby Brissett and the Ravens visit the Texans in Week 12. He threw for 276 yards with one TD and one INT and rushed twice for seven yards during Baltimore's Week 11 loss. Brissett has plenty of talented targets available to him, and it appears the Ravens are willing to continue letting it fly on offense. He'll look to get his first win with his new club versus a Houston defense allowing 20.9 fantasy points per game to opposing QBs.

free_agents.name: Isiah Pacheco
free_agents.outlook: Isiah Pacheco will be inactive again in Week 12 as the Lions play the Bears. Pacheco was placed on IR to start the season due to a back injury, and he underwent surgery in mid-September. This puts the former Kansas City RB's return this season in jeopardy. He's expected to be back sometime in December, so Sione Vaki will continue to handle RB2 duties behind Jahmyr Gibbs.

free_agents.name: Kimani Vidal
free_agents.outlook: Kimani Vidal has remained a steady part of the Chargers' game plan in recent weeks. The third-year running back has handled at least eight touches in five of the last six games, managing 167 rushing yards and a touchdown over that stretch on 4.3 yards per carry while adding an 11-63-0 line on 15 targets. While Omarion Hampton has reasserted himself as the top back, a knee injury to Keaton Mitchell could reduce Vidal's competition for backup snaps. Vidal will try to take advantage of what volume he gets in Week 12 against a Patriots defense that's tied for 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

free_agents.name: Pat Bryant
free_agents.outlook: Pat Bryant posted modest numbers over two games since returning from an ankle injury, catching seven of nine targets for 88 yards and a touchdown. The Broncos' passing game has been sluggish all year, and with the offense leaning more heavily on rookie running back Jonah Coleman, Bo Nix hasn't been required to do too much through the air. Bryant seems to have good chemistry with the quarterback, giving him a stable floor even if his ceiling is TD-dependent. Bryant will try to stay busy in Week 12 against a Steelers secondary that ranks 12th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

free_agents.name: Drew Lock
free_agents.outlook: Drew Lock will likely return to being Seattle's backup quarterback in Week 12 versus San Francisco. Lock started each of the Seahawks past two games before the team's Week 11 bye and led his team to a pair of wins, compiling 415 passing yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions. However, Sam Darnold (quad/ribs)  is expected to return to action in Week 12 following an injury layoff, and he'll presumably reclaim his starting role from Lock. The 49ers have been middle-of-the-pack in most categories against the pass this season, but Lock probably isn't going to get a chance to test their defense barring a Darnold setback.

free_agents.name: Michael Penix Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Michael Penix is expected to continue leading the Falcons' offense into the Week 12 matchup against the Vikings. Penix has really struggled over Atlanta's last three games, averaging just 191 passing yards per game while throwing just one touchdown and six interceptions during that stretch. He will likely continue to struggle against a great Vikings defense in Week 12, as Minnesota has allowed just 14.4 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season. However, there is some hope for Penix, with Brock Purdy putting up 35 points while throwing for 255 yards and three touchdowns against the Vikings in Week 11.

free_agents.name: AJ Barner
free_agents.outlook: AJ Barner heads into Seattle's Week 12 matchup versus San Francisco amidst a stretch of consistent but quiet production. Barner has caught between two and four passes in each of his past six contests while averaging 21.2 receiving yards per game during that span. The third-year tight end actually has more rushing touchdowns (two) than receiving TDs (one) this season, as he's sometimes been deployed as a ball carrier in short-yardage situations. Barner posted a 3-20-0 receiving line on five targets against San Francisco in Week 5 during the teams' first meeting of the campaign. .

free_agents.name: Tyler Higbee
free_agents.outlook: Tyler Higbee could be an important part of the Rams' passing game against the Packers in Week 12. Higbee hasn't exceeded 17 receiving yards in his past four games, but he did catch a touchdown in his most recent appearance, Week 10 against Arizona. The Rams continue to be without star wideouts Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring), so it's been all-hands-on-deck for the team's pass catchers. However, Green Bay has been tough on tight ends this season, giving up just 5.9 fantasy points per game -- fifth-best in the league -- to the position.

free_agents.name: Malachi Fields
free_agents.outlook: Malachi Fields continued his streak of catching at least two balls in every game this season for the Giants. Fields had two receptions for 25 yards in the 23-18 win over the Jags. Fields received five targets for the game. The rookie is averaging a stout 15.6 yards per catch overall. In Week 12, the Giants will face a Colts defense allowing 220.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 14th in the NFL. However, Indy has also surrendered 20 throwing scores, which is 28th in the league.

free_agents.name: Keaton Mitchell
free_agents.outlook: Keaton Mitchell has fallen into a depth role in the Chargers' backfield. After getting double-digit touches as recently as Week 9 against the Texans, he's handled just three carries and one catch over the last two games while Omarion Hampton re-staked his claim to the No. 1 job. Mitchell also picked up a knee injury in Week 11, which could leave Kimani Vidal without any competition in the short term for the backup role. If Mitchell is able to suit up in Week 12, he'll be facing a Patriots defense that's tied for 17th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

free_agents.name: Treylon Burks
free_agents.outlook: Treylon Burks was largely held in check last game for the Commanders.  Burks caught two passes for 30 yards in the 22-20 win over the Bengals. He finished tied for fourth on the team in targets. In Week 12, Burks will face a lackluster Arizona pass defense. The Cardinals are allowing 226.4 passing yards per tilt, which is 20th in the NFL. In addition, the Cardinals have surrendered the most passing touchdowns in the league to date.

free_agents.name: Roman Wilson
free_agents.outlook: Roman Wilson and the Steelers host the Broncos on Black Friday in Week 12. He corralled three of six targets for 43 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 10 loss. Wilson made his presence felt in his first game action since Week 5, as he finished second on the team in yardage and third in targets while playing 70% of the offensive snaps. Wilson will try to continue building rapport with Aaron Rodgers versus Denver's sixth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (28.1) to WRs.

free_agents.name: Bam Knight
free_agents.outlook: Bam Knight appears to be working in a RB timeshare for the Cardinals ahead of a Week 12 clash against the Commanders. Knight logged eight touches for 45 yards in this past Sunday's loss to Kansas City, while Tyler Allgeier finished with seven touches for 23 yards. Neither back has forced his way into a workhorse role, and rookie Jeremiyah Love could be on the verge of returning from an ankle injury, so Arizona's backfield is tough to get a read on at the moment. The team's running game also doesn't have the greatest Week 12 matchup, as Washington ranks in the top half of the league with 16.4 fantasy points per game allowed to running backs so far this year.

free_agents.name: Tutu Atwell
free_agents.outlook: Tutu Atwell has a chance to buoy a depleted Rams wideout corps in Week 12 against Green Bay. Los Angeles will remain without both Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring) for the matchup, and Nacua isn't expected to return to action this year. However, Atwell wasn't effective when both star wideouts were absent Week 10 against the Cardinals, as he tallied just one catch for 31 yards on two targets. Atwell is always a big-play threat, though Green Bay has allowed just 25 receptions of 20-plus yards this season, tied for seventh-fewest in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Cooper Kupp
free_agents.outlook: Cooper Kupp continues to be touchdown-dependent for fantasy value heading into Seattle's Week 12 matchup against San Francisco. Kupp has two TD receptions over his past three games but has recorded just five catches for 73 yards on eight targets during that span. With Jaxon Smith-Njigba dominating targets in Seattle's offense, there simply hasn't been much of an opportunity for the team's other pass catchers to regularly find success. The 49ers held Kupp to two catches for 15 yards in their first matchup in Week 5, and Kupp may need to find the end zone in Week 12 to make a tangible impact for fantasy managers.

free_agents.name: Austin Ekeler
free_agents.outlook: Austin Ekeler had seven carries for 41 yards last game for Washington, though ceded the majority of touches out of the backfield to Jacory Croskey-Merritt. Bill rushed 13 times for 54 yards and a touchdown in the surprising 22-20 win over the Bengals, nearly doubling up Ekeler in terms of carries. Rachaad White dressed but did not play, likely due to a heel injury, so his status for Week 12 versus the Cardinals could also affect Ekeler's usage. Arizona is allowing 128.8 rushing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the league, so there should be room to roam if Ekeler gets the opportunity.

free_agents.name: Kaleb Johnson
free_agents.outlook: Kaleb Johnson could lead Green Bay's backfield in a Week 12 matchup against the Rams. Johnson recorded double-digit carries in back-to-back games before the Packers' bye week, and he also logged first-team reps in the team's most recent Sunday practice. If Josh Jacobs remains out with a finger injury, Johnson may be the top option for the Pack in Los Angeles. The Rams have unfortunately ranked third in fantasy points allowed to running backs.

free_agents.name: Rashod Bateman
free_agents.outlook: Rashod Bateman and the Ravens look to snap a six-game losing streak when they visit the Texans in Week 12. He hauled in two of six targets for 67 yards, including a 52-yard touchdown, during Baltimore's Week 11 defeat. Bateman finished second on the team in yardage and targets, but he's now tallied three or fewer receptions in six straight outings. Despite a great matchup against Houston's vulnerable secondary, Bateman should remain on fantasy benches.

free_agents.name: Jerry Jeudy
free_agents.outlook: Jerry Jeudy and the Browns host the Raiders for a Week 12 clash on Sunday Night Football. He caught two of four targets for 74 yards during Cleveland's 27-24 win in Week 10. Jeudy did most of his damage on a 65-yard reception, helping him finish second on the team in yardage behind Harold Fannin Jr. (91). Despite the big day, Jeudy has two or fewer catches in three straight games and should remain on waiver wires.

free_agents.name: Darnell Washington
free_agents.outlook: In Week 12, Darnell Washington and the Steelers host Denver in an AFC clash on Black Friday. He caught all three targets for 22 yards during Pittsburgh's 19-16 loss in Week 11. Washington was unable to take advantage of Aaron Rodgers' 44 pass attempts, as the former has now been limited to 27 or fewer receiving yards in eight of his 10 outings. Washington remains a risky fantasy option despite a favorable matchup versus a Broncos defense allowing 18.5 fantasy points per game (30th) to TEs

free_agents.name: Ja'Kobi Lane
free_agents.outlook: Ja'Kobi Lane and the Ravens are in Houston for an AFC clash in Week 12. Despite playing 49% of the offensive snaps during Baltimore's Week 11 defeat, Lane was not targeted in the passing game. One week after earning a career-high 11 targets in Jacoby Brissett's team debut, the rookie receiver was unable to establish further chemistry with his new QB. Lane could take advantage of a Texans defense allowing 35.7 fantasy points per game (27th) to WRs, but he's best left on fantasy benches for now.

free_agents.name: Ryan Fitzgerald
free_agents.outlook: Ryan Fitzgerald will likely have plenty of scoring chances during Carolina's Week 12 matchup against the Buccaneers. Fitzgerald was perfect during the Week 11 win over the Ravens, converting on both field goals and all three extra points. On the season, Fitzgerald has made 17 of 19 field-goal attempts and 21 of 16 point-after tries. He could see loads of scoring chances in Week 12, as Tampa Bay's defense has allowed 7.7 kicking points per game this season.

free_agents.name: Dawson Knox
free_agents.outlook: Dawson Knox could benefit if he's again the Bills' top tight end with Dalton Kincaid's availability in question ahead of the Bills' Week 12 matchup with the Chiefs. Knox didn't garner much attention in Week 11 with Kincaid out, catching two of three targets for 31 yards. Even with more reps, his main job was blocking. Kansas City has been vulnerable to tight ends, allowing five touchdown receptions in 10 outings and the seventh-most fantasy points per game. If Kincaid misses Week 12's Thanksgiving affair, Knox becomes a deep league streamer.

free_agents.name: Jack Bech
free_agents.outlook: Jack Bech continues to show intriguing chemistry with rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza. In two games since Mendoza replaced Kirk Cousins under center, Bech has turned 16 targets into a 10-98-1 line with most of that production coming in a Week 11 loss to the Broncos. The second-year wide receiver missed four games earlier this year with a forearm injury but he appears to be fully recovered and ready to flash the upside that made him a third-round pick in 2025. Bech will face a Browns secondary in Week 12 that ranks 14th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

free_agents.name: Trey Smack
free_agents.outlook: Trey Smack will aim to lock in out of the bye as the Packers play the Rams in Week 12. Smack missed another kick in a Week 10 loss to the Vikings, which has been his norm for a lot of this season. Smack has gone 15-for-21 on field-goal attempts and missed three of his 24 XPAs across 10 games. He'll face a Los Angeles squad that's ranked 25th in fantasy points allowed to kickers.

free_agents.name: Kalif Raymond
free_agents.outlook: Kalif Raymond remains a depth option in Chicago's passing offense ahead of Week 12 at Detroit. Raymond struggled to do much with four targets in a Week 11 win over New Orleans, converting them into one catch for 14 yards. The veteran has now caught just 7 of his 14 targets in the Bears' last four outings. He'll face a Lions defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs this campaign.

free_agents.name: Andre Szmyt
free_agents.outlook: Andre Szmyt and the Browns hope to remain undefeated at home when they host the Raiders on Sunday Night Football in Week 12. He went 2-for-3 on field goal attempts and made all three PATs during Cleveland's Week 10 win. Szmyt's miss came from 54 yards, marking his first misfire on four attempts from that range this season. The Browns have scored at least 22 points in three of their last four outings, and they'll try to do so again versus a Las Vegas defense that is allowing 29.7 points per game, the most in the league.

free_agents.name: Darius Cooper
free_agents.outlook: Darius Cooper was the surprise leading receiver last game for the Eagles. Cooper managed four catches for a team-high 59 yards in the 19-16 win over the Steelers. He finished second on the team in targets for the contest, and only three other players caught passes from quarterback Joe Milton.  Cooper could find more success in Week 12 versus a porous Dallas Cowboys defense. Dallas is allowing 237.9 passing yards per tilt, which is 28th in the league. "America's Team" has also given up 21 passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 29th in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Mason Taylor
free_agents.outlook: Mason Taylor's involvement in the Jets' low-volume passing game remains limited ahead of a Week 12 clash with the Dolphins. He has been held to 25 yards or fewer in seven of nine games this season, drawing just 31 targets on the year. He provided a spike week of five catches, 62 yards, and two touchdowns against Miami in Week 7, but his usage and form don't portend a repeat against a defense that's allowing 8.0 yards per target to tight ends but only four additional touchdowns outside of Taylor's prior effort.

free_agents.name: Kayshon Boutte
free_agents.outlook: Kayshon Boutte injured his hip in Week 11. Though the injury doesn't appear to be too serious, which suggests he could suit up in Week 12 against the Ravens, if Boutte plays, he'll be a high-risk, high-reward fantasy option best utilized in deeper leagues. He had 125 yards and two TDs in Week 9 against the Chargers, as well as 40 yards and a TD prior to getting hurt in Week 11 against the Colts, but Boutte has just 194 yards in eight other appearances for the Texans.

free_agents.name: Calvin Ridley
free_agents.outlook: Calvin Ridley stepped up in the first game after Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) was lost for the season, as the veteran WR caught five of six targets for 68 yards and a touchdown in the Titans' Week 11 loss to Dallas. Prior to that game, Ridley had just six catches for 91 yards and no TDs all season. Carnell Tate and Chimere Dike will likely remain ahead of Ridley in the pecking order at WR, but Ridley could push Elic Ayomanor for playing time on the outside in a Titans passing game that has been closer to league-average in the last three games after posting bottom-three numbers for most of the season. Ridley could be worth a speculative add in deeper formats, though he remains hard to trust in Week 12 against the heavily favored Jaguars.

free_agents.name: Drew Stevens
free_agents.outlook: Drew Stevens had a banner day for Washington in the stunning 22-20 win over the Bengals.  Stevens connected on five field goals, including the game-winner. It was the third time in four games that Stevens connected on multiple field goals. The rookie has made 22 of 25 three-pointers in all this season. With the Washington offense looking better behind a healthy Jayden Daniels, Stevens could be primed for another outstanding output in Week 12 versus the Cardinals. Arizona is allowing 29.4 points per tilt, which is 31st in the league.

free_agents.name: Chimere Dike
free_agents.outlook: Chimere Dike has led Tennessee's wide receivers in receiving yards twice in the past three games, posting 71 yards in Week 8 against the Bengals and 69 yards in Week 11 against the Cowboys. He was held to just 16 receiving yards by the Jaguars in between, and Dike will face Jacksonville again in a Week 12 road rematch. He looks poised to remain a staple in three-receiver sets while working out of the slot since Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) has been ruled out for the remainder of the season. Dike has shown enough in recent weeks to earn flex consideration against a Jacksonville defense that is around league-average against WRs but excels at stopping the run.

free_agents.name: Cade Otton
free_agents.outlook: Cade Otton is expected to remain Tampa Bay's top tight end during the Week 12 matchup against the Panthers. Otton was underwhelming during the Week 11 loss to the Lions, catching just one of three targets for eight yards. He's tallied one-or-fewer receptions in four of the Buccaneers' last five games, making him almost impossible to trust for fantasy purposes going forward. Additionally, Otton is in for a tough Week 12 matchup against a Panthers defense that's allowed just 12.1 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.

free_agents.name: Tre' Harris
free_agents.outlook: Tre' Harris has caught multiple passes in four straight games since the Chargers' Week 7 bye, posting a 13-151-0 line on 17 targets over that stretch. The second-year wide receiver's skill set seems to be a better fit for Mike McDaniel's offense than Quentin Johnston's as the duo battles for the No. 2 role behind Ladd McConkey, but neither offers much upside in a struggling passing game. Justin Herbert is also in the concussion protocol, and DJ Uiagalelei could wind up making his first career NFL start, putting a further damper on the offense. Harris will be a risky play in Week 12, even against a Patriots secondary that ranks an enticing 31st in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

free_agents.name: Joe Milton
free_agents.outlook: Joe Milton guided the Eagles to victory last game, though his numbers were rather pedestrian. Milton threw for 141 yards and rushed for just seven more in the 19-16 win over the Steelers. He has yet to throw a touchdown through two starts. That could change in Week 12, though, as he faces the porous defense of his former squad, the Dallas Cowboys. "America's Team" has given up 21 passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 29th in the NFL. Dallas is also allowing 237.9 passing yards per tilt, which is 28th in the league.

free_agents.name: Jake Elliott
free_agents.outlook: Jake Elliott is coming off perhaps his best game of the season for the Eagles. Elliott nailed all four of his field goals as well as an extra point in the 19-16 win over the Steelers. Two of Elliott's makes came from over 50 yards out. It was just the second time all season Elliott connected on more than one field goal in a game. He will look to keep rolling in Week 12 versus a suspect Dallas defense. The Cowboys are allowing 28.4 points per tilt, which is 29th in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Roschon Johnson
free_agents.outlook: Roschon Johnson will look to get back to full health as the Bears play the Lions in Week 12. Johnson hurt his ankle in the first quarter of Week 11 against the Saints and was unable to return to the matchup. While the return of Kyle Monangai was likely to diminish Johnson's role, he does have value as a change-of-pace option. IF he is able to return to the field, he'll face a Detroit defense that's ranked fifth in fantasy points allowed to RBs.

free_agents.name: Jauan Jennings
free_agents.outlook: Jauan Jennings will look to stay involved as the Vikings play the Falcons in Week 12. Jennings recorded a season-high three catches in a Week 11 loss to the 49ers, and he converted them for 20 yards. With Jordan Addison likely to be out for another week with a thumb injury, Jennings could continue to see an increase in targets. He'll face an Atlanta defense that's ranked 25th in fantasy points allowed to WRs this campaign.

free_agents.name: Will Shipley
free_agents.outlook: Will Shipley managed four touches last game for the Eagles. With Saquon Barkley nursing a left arm injury for the final eight minutes of the win over the Steelers, Shipley saw four carries for nine yards. Barkley should be healthy enough to suit up on Thanksgiving versus the Cowboys, though. If Shipley is needed, he could have sneaky value against a Dallas defense that has been abysmal against the run in 2026.  The Cowboys are allowing 151.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is the worst mark in the NFL. In addition, Dallas has given up 15 rushing scores, which is 29th in the league.

free_agents.name: Evan Engram
free_agents.outlook: Evan Engram is coming off his most productive game of the season in the Broncos' Week 11 win over the Raiders. The veteran tight end set new season highs in catches, targets, and receiving yards with a 6-74-0 line on eight looks from Bo Nix. However, Engram missed his chance to score his first touchdown since Week 1 when Adam Trautman vultured a one-yard TD on his only catch. Engram had managed just seven catches for 48 yards over his prior four games combined. He'll remain a volatile option in Week 12 against a Steelers defense that ranks 14th in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

free_agents.name: Ted Hurst III
free_agents.outlook: Ted Hurst will look to build on an impressive performance in Tampa Bay's Week 12 matchup against the Panthers. Hurst was the Buccaneers' most productive receiver during the Week 11 loss to the Lions, catching five of seven targets for 56 yards and two touchdowns. He also played 63% of the team's offensive snaps after playing just one the game prior, suggesting his role is growing as the year progresses. Despite this, Hurst could struggle in Week 12 against a Carolina secondary that's given up just 9.5 yards per reception this year, the fourth-best mark in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Jalen Nailor
free_agents.outlook: Jalen Nailor remains ineffective as a pass catcher for the Raiders, despite the team's switch at quarterback. In two games since rookie Fernando Mendoza replaced Kirk Cousins under center, Nailor has caught just two of nine targets for 15 yards. Jack Bech appears to be Mendoza's preferred option among the wide receiver corps, and Brock Bowers should command plenty of attention once he returns to the lineup. Nailor's blocking skills will keep him on the field, but he offers little upside in Week 12 against a Browns secondary that ranks 14th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

free_agents.name: Jahan Dotson
free_agents.outlook: Jahan Dotson is expected to operate as Atlanta's No. 2 wideout during the Week 12 matchup against the Vikings. Dotson has emerged as one of the Falcons' top pass catchers over the last five games, catching 11 of 21 targets for 267 yards and a touchdown during that span. Despite this, he likely won't be fantasy relevant without finding the end zone while playing behind Drake London. Dotson is expected to struggle in Week 12 against a tough Minnesota secondary that's allowed just six touchdowns to opposing wideouts this season.
